body.translated_text: The first <s>stotra</s> (hymn) named <s>Bhaktivilāsa</s> (The Play of Devotion)
<s>Oṃ</s>

body.text: na dhyāyato na japataḥ syād yasyāvidhipūrvakam &

children.text: evam eva śivabhāsas taṃ numo bhaktiśālinam // UtSst_1.1 //
children.translated_text: who shines forth as <s>Śiva</s> spontaneously — we bow to that one who is endowed with <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). // 1.1 //

body.translated_text: One for whom it arises without any prescribed method, neither through meditation nor through recitation,

children.text: lokayātrārajorāgāt palitair iva dhūsaraḥ // UtSst_1.2 //
children.translated_text: is grey as if with white hairs from the dust-stain of worldly activity. // 1.2 //

body.translated_text: My <s>ātman</s> (self), though rejuvenated by drinking the nectar of devotion to You,

children.text: saṃcāro lokamārge 'pi syāt tayaiva vijṛmbhayā // UtSst_1.3 //
children.translated_text: even their movement on the worldly path would be by that very expansion of devotion alone. // 1.3 //

body.translated_text: For the devoted ones dwelling in Your city who have attained that wealth,

children.text: kiṃ na bhaktimatāṃ kṣetram mantraḥ kvaiṣām na siddhyati // UtSst_1.4 //
children.translated_text: what place is not a sacred field for the devoted? Where does their <s>mantra</s> not bear fruit? // 1.4 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, in this entire world which is directly pervaded by You,

children.text: advitīyā api sadā tvaddvitīyā api prabho // UtSst_1.5 //
children.translated_text: who, though non-dual, are always paired with You, O Lord! // 1.5 //

body.translated_text: Glorious are those intoxicated by the excellent liquor of the nectar-essence of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion),

body.text: anantānandasindhos te nātha tattvaṃ vidanti te &

children.text: tādṛśa eva ye sāndrabhaktyānandarasāplutāḥ // UtSst_1.6 //
children.translated_text: those very ones who are immersed in the dense bliss-essence of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). // 1.6 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, they know the true nature of You, the ocean of infinite bliss —

body.text: tvam evātmeśa sarvasya sarvaś cātmani rāgavān &

children.text: iti svabhāvasiddhāṃs tvadbhaktiṃ jānañ jayej janaḥ // UtSst_1.7 //
children.translated_text: knowing this devotion to You as naturally established, one would conquer, O people! // 1.7 //

body.translated_text: You alone are the Self of all, O Lord, and all have love for You within the Self —

body.text: nātha vedyakṣaye kena na dṛśyo 'syekakaḥ sthitaḥ &

children.text: vedyavedakasaṃkṣobhe 'py asi bhaktaiḥ sudarśanaḥ // UtSst_1.8 //
children.translated_text: Even in the agitation of knower and known, You are easily seen by the devoted. // 1.8 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when the knowable is dissolved, by whom are You not seen, standing alone?

children.text: aviyuktāsti te tadvad ekā tvadbhaktir astu me // UtSst_1.9 //
children.translated_text: is ever inseparable from You — so may I have that one singular devotion to You. // 1.9 //

body.translated_text: As the beloved goddess, a lake of infinite bliss,

children.text: saṃvinmārgo 'yam āhlādaduḥkhamohais tridhā sthitaḥ // UtSst_1.10 //
children.translated_text: this path of <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), standing in three modes as delight, sorrow, and delusion. // 1.10 //

body.translated_text: For the devoted, O all-pervading Lord, everything is a means to attaining You —

children.text: daśā sā māṃ prati svāmin nāsavasyeva śuktatā // UtSst_1.11 //
children.translated_text: would be to me, O Master, like the sourness of wine that has turned to vinegar. // 1.11 //

body.translated_text: From savoring the nectar of devotion to You, even the supreme state of <s>bodha</s> (awakening)

children.text: vidyāvidyobhayasyāpi tā ete tattvavedinaḥ // UtSst_1.12 //
children.translated_text: they are the knowers of reality, of both <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // 1.12 //

body.translated_text: Those for whom the great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) of devotion to You has become practiced —

children.text: tvadbhaktisudhayā siktā tadrasāḍhyaphalāstu me // UtSst_1.13 //
children.translated_text: watered by the nectar of devotion to You, bear fruit rich with that essence for me. // 1.13 //

body.translated_text: May this creeper of speech, unfolding gradually from its root,

body.text: śivo bhūtvā yajeteti bhakto bhūtveti kathyate &

children.text: tvam eva hi vapuḥ sāraṃ bhaktair advayaśodhitam // UtSst_1.14 //
children.translated_text: for You alone are the essential body, purified as non-dual by the devoted. // 1.14 //

body.translated_text: "Having become <s>Śiva</s>, one should worship" — this is stated as "having become a devotee,"

children.text: tadasiddhyai nikṛṣṭānāṃ kāni nāvaraṇāni vā // UtSst_1.15 //
children.translated_text: And for the debased, what coverings are there not preventing that attainment? // 1.15 //

body.translated_text: For the devoted, what reasonings are there not to establish non-duality with You?

children.text: anyathā sarvakakṣyāsu bhāsi bhaktimatāṃ katham // UtSst_1.16 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, how do You shine in all stages for the devoted? // 1.16 //

body.translated_text: "You are attainable only sometimes, somewhere, through <s>yoga</s>" — this is deception, O Lord!

children.text: yogibhyo bhaktibhājām yad vyutthāne 'pi samāhitāḥ // UtSst_1.17 //
children.translated_text: for the devotees over the <s>yogins</s>: that they are absorbed even in ordinary activity. // 1.17 //

body.translated_text: Untouched by <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses) and such practices, this great distinction exists

body.text: na yogo na tapo nārcākramaḥ ko 'pi pranīyate &

children.text: amāye śivamārge 'smin bhaktir ekā praśasyate // UtSst_1.18 //
children.translated_text: on this guileless path of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) alone is praised. // 1.18 //

body.translated_text: No <s>yoga</s>, no <s>tapas</s> (austerity), no elaborate course of ritual worship is prescribed;

children.text: pratyakṣasarvabhāvasya cintānām api naśyatu // UtSst_1.19 //
children.translated_text: for whom all things are directly manifest — may even the need for thought perish! // 1.19 //

body.translated_text: For me, whose veil is destroyed by the radiance of devotion blazing on all sides,

body.text: śiva ity ekaśabdasya jihvāgre tiṣṭhataḥ sadā &

children.text: samastaviṣayāsvādo bhakteṣv evāsti ko 'py aho // UtSst_1.20 //
children.translated_text: there is in the devoted an extraordinary relish of all sense objects — how wondrous! // 1.20 //

body.translated_text: With the single word "<s>Śiva</s>" always resting on the tip of the tongue,

children.text: alaukikarasāsvāde susthaiḥ ko 'nāma gaṇyate // UtSst_1.21 //
children.translated_text: in that unworldly savoring of <s>rasa</s> (essence), who among the steadfast would even be counted? // 1.21 //

body.translated_text: In the ocean of the nectar of devotion — peaceful, wave-stilled, cool, clear, and sweet —

children.text: tādṛśī bhagavan yasyā mokṣākhyo 'nantaro rasaḥ // UtSst_1.22 //
children.translated_text: O Blessed Lord, whose immediate after-taste is called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)? // 1.22 //

body.translated_text: Why would one not chew with relish the great medicine of devotion to You,

body.text: tā eva paramarthyante sampadaḥ sadbhir īśa yāḥ &

children.text: tvad bhaktirasasambhogavisrambhaparipoṣikāḥ // UtSst_1.23 //
children.translated_text: which nourish the confidence of enjoying the essence of devotion to You. // 1.23 //

body.translated_text: Only those attainments are truly valued by the wise, O Lord,

children.text: ye na rāgādi paṅke 'smiṃḷ lipyante patitā api // UtSst_1.24 //
children.translated_text: they are not stained by the mud of <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the rest, even when they have fallen in it. // 1.24 //

body.translated_text: Marked by some ineffable essence of the nectar of devotion to You,

children.text: bhavadbhakter vipakvāyā latāyā iva keṣu cit // UtSst_1.25 //
children.translated_text: only to certain limbs, as it were, of the fully ripened creeper of devotion to You. // 1.25 //

body.translated_text: From <s>aṇimā</s> (subtlety) and the other powers up to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), the designation "fruit" applies

body.text: citraṃ nisargato nātha duḥkhabījam idaṃ manaḥ &

children.text: tvadbhaktirasasaṃsiktam niḥśreyasamahāphalam // UtSst_1.26 //
children.translated_text: when irrigated by the essence of devotion to You, bears the great fruit of the highest good. // 1.26 //

body.translated_text: Wondrous! O Lord, this mind which is by nature a seed of suffering,
The second <s>stotra</s> (hymn) named <s>Sarvātmaparibhāvanā</s> (Contemplation of the Universal Self)

children.text: svarūpa bahurūpāya namaḥ saṃvinmayāya te // UtSst_2.1 //
children.translated_text: homage to You of many forms, who are made of <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness)! // 2.1 //

body.translated_text: O You whose form is <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun), <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the stationary and the moving —

children.text: mahānalāya bhavate viśvaikahaviṣe namaḥ // UtSst_2.2 //
children.translated_text: homage to You, the great fire, for whom the entire universe is the single oblation! // 2.2 //

body.translated_text: To You of great radiance, purified by the anointing of the great alkaline ash of universal fuel,

children.text: kasmai cid viśvasaṃploṣaviṣamāya namo 'stu te // UtSst_2.3 //
children.translated_text: yet somehow terribly fierce in the conflagration of the universe — homage to You! // 2.3 //

body.translated_text: To You who are dense with supreme nectar, cool, the fire of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: maheśvarāyāpi namaḥ kasmai cin mantramūrtaye // UtSst_2.4 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Maheśvara</s> also — homage to that certain one whose form is <s>mantra</s>! // 2.4 //

body.translated_text: To <s>Mahādeva</s>, to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, to <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: vasekaviṣamāyāpi maṅgalāya śivāgnaye // UtSst_2.5 //
children.translated_text: drenched in the dripping fat of the three worlds, cut and dried up. // 2.5 //

body.translated_text: Homage to the fire of <s>Śiva</s>, who is auspicious even while terrifying,

children.text: tasmai namo 'stu devāya kasmai cid api śambhave // UtSst_2.6 //
children.translated_text: to that god, to some ineffable <s>Śambhu</s>, homage! // 2.6 //

body.translated_text: He whose distinguishing mark is precisely the absence of all distinguishing marks —

children.text: vedāgamasatattvāya guhyāya svāmine namaḥ // UtSst_2.7 //
children.translated_text: who is the true essence of the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s> — homage to the secret Lord! // 2.7 //

body.translated_text: To Him who contradicts the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s>, who is the author of the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s>,

children.text: namaḥ samsārarūpāya niḥsaṃsārāya śambhave // UtSst_2.8 //
children.translated_text: homage to <s>Śambhu</s>, whose form is <s>saṃsāra</s> itself, yet who is beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>! // 2.8 //

body.translated_text: To Him who is the sole cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclical existence), the sole adversary of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: kṣīnāgramadhyamūlāya namaḥ pūrṇāya śambhave // UtSst_2.9 //
children.translated_text: to Him in whom root, middle, and summit have vanished — homage to the complete <s>Śambhu</s>! // 2.9 //

body.translated_text: To the root, the middle, and the summit; to Him whose form is root, middle, and summit;

children.text: yasya nāmagrahas tasmai durlabhāya śivāya te // UtSst_2.10 //
children.translated_text: is the fruit of accumulated merit — to that rare and precious <s>Śiva</s>, homage to You! // 2.10 //

body.translated_text: Homage! Even a single utterance of His name

children.text: krīḍate tubhyam ekasmai cinmayāya kapāline // UtSst_2.11 //
children.translated_text: who forever sports with the multitudes of corpses in the form of moving and unmoving beings! // 2.11 //

body.translated_text: Homage to You, the one who is of the nature of consciousness, the skull-bearer,

children.text: sūkṣmāya viśvarūpāya namaś citrāya śambhave // UtSst_2.12 //
children.translated_text: to the subtle, to the one whose form is the universe — homage to the wondrous <s>Śambhu</s>! // 2.12 //

body.translated_text: To the wielder of <s>māyā</s> (illusion), to the utterly pure, to the hidden, to the self-manifest,

children.text: āścaryakaraṇīyāya namas te sarvaśaktaye // UtSst_2.13 //
children.translated_text: to the worker of marvels — homage to You, the omnipotent one! // 2.13 //

body.translated_text: To Him whose sport is the dissolution of the world deployed through <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

body.text: taṭeṣv eva paribhrāntaiḥ labdhās tās tā vibhūtayaḥ &

children.text: yasya tasmai namas tubhyam agādhaharasindhave // UtSst_2.14 //
children.translated_text: of that which is You — homage to You, the unfathomable ocean of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva)! // 2.14 //

body.translated_text: Those various powers obtained by those who have only wandered along the shores

children.text: alepāya namaḥ śambhuśatapatrāya śobhine // UtSst_2.15 //
children.translated_text: yet is unstained — homage to the radiant lotus that is <s>Śambhu</s>! // 2.15 //

body.translated_text: To Him who dwells in the midst of the thick mud of the world made of <s>māyā</s> (illusion),

children.text: priyāya paramārthāya sarvotkṛṣṭāya te namaḥ // UtSst_2.16 //
children.translated_text: to the beloved, to the ultimate reality, to the most exalted — homage to You! // 2.16 //

body.translated_text: To the auspicious, to the purifier, to the treasure, to Him whose nature is adornment,

children.text: bandhamokṣavihīnāya kasmai ci d api śambhave // UtSst_2.17 //
children.translated_text: who is devoid of both bondage and liberation — to some ineffable <s>Śambhu</s>! // 2.17 //

body.translated_text: Homage to Him who is eternally bound, who forever partakes of liberation,

children.text: tubhyam evādvitīyāya namo nityasukhāsine // UtSst_2.18 //
children.translated_text: homage to You alone, the non-dual, ever seated in bliss! // 2.18 //

body.translated_text: In this entire triple world whose essence is but a jest,

children.text: sarvācārāya śarvāya nirācārāya te namaḥ // UtSst_2.19 //
children.translated_text: to the follower of all paths, to <s>Śarva</s>, to the one beyond all paths — homage to You! // 2.19 //

body.translated_text: To the essence of the right-hand path, to the one who delights in the left-hand path,

body.text: yathā tathāpi yaḥ pūjyo yatra tatrāpi yo 'rcitaḥ &

children.text: yo 'pi vā so 'pi vā yo 'sau devas tasmai namo 'stu te // UtSst_2.20 //
children.translated_text: whoever He may be, however He may be — to that God, homage to You! // 2.20 //

body.translated_text: He who is to be worshipped however one worships, who is honored wherever one honors,

children.text: namo vitatalāvaṇyavarāya varadāya te // UtSst_2.21 //
children.translated_text: homage to You, the bestower of boons, resplendent with boundless beauty! // 2.21 //

body.translated_text: To Him who is served by those seeking liberation, who removes all torments,

children.text: trilokāya namas tubhyaṃ svāmine nityaparvaṇe // UtSst_2.22 //
children.translated_text: filled with the essence of bliss — homage to You, O Master of eternal festival! // 2.22 //

body.translated_text: To You who are always, without interruption, the entire three worlds

children.text: tvām eva tasmai ghorāya śaktivṛndāya te namaḥ // UtSst_2.23 //
children.translated_text: You alone — homage to that fierce host of <s>Śaktis</s> (powers) which is You! // 2.23 //

body.translated_text: And that through experiences predominantly of pleasure one worships

children.text: āliṅganty api yaṃ tasmai kasmai cid bhavate namaḥ // UtSst_2.24 //
children.translated_text: even embrace Him — homage to that certain one, to You! // 2.24 //

body.translated_text: He who is unknowable even to sages, yet those whose actions are characterized by devotion

children.text: sarvapāramyapāramyaprāpyāya bhavate namaḥ // UtSst_2.25 //
children.translated_text: to Him who is attainable at the uttermost limit of all supremacy — homage to You! // 2.25 //

body.translated_text: To the treasury of supreme nectar, to the abundance of supreme nectar,

children.text: apūrvamodasubhagaṃ parāmṛtarasolvaṇam // UtSst_2.26 //
children.translated_text: graced with unprecedented delight, brimming with the essence of supreme nectar. // 2.26 //

body.translated_text: I praise Your form, made of the great <s>mantra</s>, clear and cool,

children.text: citraṃ nāsty eva yatreśa tan naumi tava śāsanam // UtSst_2.27 //
children.translated_text: where nothing is wondrous, O Lord — that sovereignty of Yours I praise. // 2.27 //

body.translated_text: On the great canvas of the proclamation of Your unity with the fullness of the nectar of freedom,

children.text: sarvāmaṅgalyakalpāntaṃ mārgaṃ māheśvaraṃ numaḥ // UtSst_2.28 //
children.translated_text: the end of all ages for all inauspiciousness — we praise the <s>Māheśvara</s> (Śaiva) path! // 2.28 //

body.translated_text: The thunderbolt against all doubt, the apocalyptic fire against all misfortune,

body.text: jaya deva namo namo 'stu te sakalaṃ viśvam idaṃ tavāśritam &

children.text: jagatāṃ parameśvaro bhavān paramekaḥ śaraṇāgato 'smi te // UtSst_2.29 //
children.translated_text: You are the supreme Lord of all worlds, the supreme one — I have come to Your refuge. // 2.29 //

body.translated_text: Victory, O God! Homage, homage to You! This entire universe depends on You;
The third <s>stotra</s> (hymn) named <s>Praṇayaprasāda</s> (The Grace of Loving Devotion)

body.text: sadasattvena bhāvānāṃ yuktā yā dvitayī gatiḥ &

children.text: tām ullaṅghya tṛtīyasmai namaś citrāya śambhave // UtSst_3.1 //
children.translated_text: transcending that, homage to the wondrous <s>Śambhu</s> who is the third! // 3.1 //

body.translated_text: The dual condition that pertains to things through being existent and non-existent —

children.text: svatantrās te svatantrasya ye tavaivānujīvinaḥ // UtSst_3.2 //
children.translated_text: those who are free are free because they are Your dependents, O sovereign one! // 3.2 //

body.translated_text: In this triple world which is not autonomous, from the race of demons to that of sages,

children.text: yeṣām bhavarujām ekaṃ bheṣajaṃ te sukhāsinaḥ // UtSst_3.3 //
children.translated_text: is the one medicine for the disease of existence — they for whom this is so sit in ease. // 3.3 //

body.translated_text: The recollection of Your body, studded with the entire universe,

children.text: cāmaraṃ svardhunīsrotaḥ sa ekaḥ parameśvaraḥ // UtSst_3.4 //
children.translated_text: whose <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk) is the stream of the <s>Svardhunī</s> (celestial Ganges) — He alone is the supreme Lord. // 3.4 //

body.translated_text: He whose white parasol is the moon filled with its own radiance,

body.text: prakāśāṃ śītalām ekāṃ śuddhāṃ śaśikalām iva &

children.text: dṛśaṃ vitara me nātha kām apy amṛtavāhinīm // UtSst_3.5 //
children.translated_text: like a digit of the moon — some ineffable bearer of nectar. // 3.5 //

body.translated_text: Bestow upon me, O Lord, a gaze that is luminous, cool, singular, and pure,

children.text: imāḥ kathaṃ me bhagavan nāmṛtāsvādasundarāḥ // UtSst_3.6 //
children.translated_text: how could they not be beautiful with the taste of nectar, O Blessed Lord? // 3.6 //

body.translated_text: These drops of consciousness that have fallen from the ocean of Your <s>cit</s> (consciousness) and <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) —

body.text: tvayi rāgarase nātha na magnaṃ hṛdayaṃ prabho &

children.text: yeṣām ahṛdayā eva te 'vajñaspadam īdṛśāḥ // UtSst_3.7 //
children.translated_text: they are indeed heartless, and as such are objects of contempt. // 3.7 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, O Master, those whose hearts are not immersed in the essence of passion for You —

children.text: prābhavīṇāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ paramekaḥ sa bhājanam // UtSst_3.8 //
children.translated_text: he alone is the supreme vessel of Your sovereign powers. // 3.8 //

body.translated_text: He with whom the Lord, You, has formed a heart-union —

body.text: harṣāṇām atha śokānāṃ sarveṣāṃ plāvakaḥ samam &

children.text: bhavaddhyānāmṛtāpūro nimnāṇimnabhuvām iva // UtSst_3.9 //
children.translated_text: the flood of the nectar of meditation on You fills the low and the high alike. // 3.9 //

body.translated_text: Equally flooding all joys and all sorrows,

body.text: keva na syād dṛśā teṣāṃ sukhasambhāranirbharā &

children.text: yeṣām ātmādhikeneśa na kvāpi virahas tvayā // UtSst_3.10 //
children.translated_text: who are never anywhere separated from You even more than from their own self, O Lord? // 3.10 //

body.translated_text: Who would not be content with the gaze of those, brimming with an abundance of happiness,

body.text: garjāmi bata nṛtyāmi pūrṇā mama manorathāḥ &

children.text: svāmī mamaiṣa ghaṭito yat tvam atyantarocanaḥ // UtSst_3.11 //
children.translated_text: For this master has been united with me — You, who are supremely delightful! // 3.11 //

body.translated_text: I roar! I dance! My desires are fulfilled!

body.text: nānyad vedyaṃ kriyā yatra nānyo yogo vidā ca yat &

children.text: jñānaṃ syāt kiṃ tu viśvaikapūrṇā cittvaṃ vijṛmbhate // UtSst_3.12 //
children.translated_text: what knowledge could there be? Rather, Your being consciousness, full of the entire universe, unfolds. // 3.12 //

body.translated_text: Where there is nothing else to be known, nor any other action, nor any other <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: hastāt palāyitā yeṣāṃ vāci śaśvacchivadhvaniḥ // UtSst_3.13 //
children.translated_text: of those in whose speech the sound of "<s>Śiva</s>" eternally resounds. // 3.13 //

body.translated_text: The unconquerable, endless sorrows flee instantly from the hands

children.text: tvaṃ mahāpuruṣas tv eko niḥśeṣapuruṣāśrayaḥ // UtSst_3.14 //
children.translated_text: but You are the one great Person, the support of all persons without remainder. // 3.14 //

children.translated_text: those for whom this very ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is a great lake of sport. // 3.15 //

children.translated_text: "In truth, recite!" — thus You indicate somewhere with a rosary of beads. // 3.17 //

children.translated_text: You are other than both the non-existent and the existent, therefore You are comprised of both being and non-being. // 3.18 //

children.text: api tvaṃ sarvabhuvanavyāpako 'pi na dṛśyase // UtSst_3.19 //
children.translated_text: though pervading all worlds, You are not seen. // 3.19 //

body.translated_text: Though possessing a pure radiance surpassing the rays of a thousand suns,

body.text: jaḍe jagati cidrūpaḥ kila vedye 'pi vedakaḥ &

children.text: vibhur mite ca yenāsi tena sarvottamo bhavān // UtSst_3.20 //
children.translated_text: You are all-pervading in the limited — by this You are the supreme being. // 3.20 //

The fourth <s>stotra</s> (hymn) named <s>Surasodbalā</s> (The Exaltation of the Gods)

children.translated_text: the beloved of <s>Ambikā</s>, the Guru of the three worlds, the refuge of even those who are themselves refuges. // 4.1 //

children.text: āśrityāpy adharatarāṃ bhūmiṃ nādyāpi citram ujjhāmi // UtSst_4.2 //
children.translated_text: even though I have resorted to a lower ground, even now I do not abandon this wonder. // 4.2 //

body.translated_text: Having leapt over the ladder of steps leading to the various deities, and having reached the feet of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: yāvad bhavāmi bhagavaṃs tava sapadi sadodito dāsaḥ // UtSst_4.3 //
children.translated_text: so that I may swiftly become Your servant, ever risen and devoted. // 4.3 //

body.translated_text: Reveal Your own path, O Lord, conceal all the more the ways of the entire world,

body.text: śiva śiva śambho śaṅkara śaraṇāgatavatsalāśu kuru karuṇām &

children.text: tava caraṇakamalayugalasmaraṇaparasya hi sampado 'dūre // UtSst_4.4 //
children.translated_text: For one devoted to the remembrance of Your pair of lotus feet, prosperity is not far away. // 4.4 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>! O You who are tender to those who seek refuge, quickly bestow compassion!

children.text: te viriñcim adhikāramalenāliptam asvavaśam īśa hasanti // UtSst_4.5 //
children.translated_text: they laugh at <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), who is stained by the impurity of his office and not master of himself, O Lord! // 4.5 //

body.translated_text: Those who, seated on the lotus-throne of Your feet, create the world as they please,

body.text: tvatprakāśavapuṣo na vibhinnaṃ kiṃ cana prabhavati pratibhātum &

children.text: tat sadaiva bhagavan parilabdho 'sīśvara prakṛtito 'pi vidūraḥ // UtSst_4.6 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O Blessed Lord, You are always attained, O Lord, though by nature You are utterly remote. // 4.6 //

body.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever can appear as separate from Your body which is luminous radiance;

body.text: pādapaṅkajarasaṃ tava ke cid bhedaparyuṣitavṛttim upetāḥ &

children.text: ke canāpi rasayanti tu sadhyo bhātam akṣatavapur dvayaśūnyam // UtSst_4.7 //
children.translated_text: But some indeed savor that which shines forth immediately, with body undiminished, free from duality. [UtSst 4.7]

body.translated_text: Some, having attained the essence of Your lotus feet, yet having adopted a disposition stale with duality,

body.text: nātha vidyud iva bhāti vibhāte yā kadā cana mamāmṛtadigdhā &

children.text: sā yadi sthirataraiva bhavet tat pūjito 'si vidhivat kim utānyat // UtSst_4.8 //
children.translated_text: if only that were more stable — then you would be worshipped in the proper manner; what more need be said? [UtSst 4.8]

body.translated_text: O Lord, that which sometimes flashes forth in the dawn like lightning, anointed with nectar for me,

body.text: sarvam asyaparam asti na kiṃ cid vastv avastu yadi veti mahatyā &

children.text: prajñāya vyavasito 'tra yathaiva tvaṃ tathaiva bhava suprakaṭo me // UtSst_4.9 //
children.translated_text: wisdom having been determined thus, just as you are, so be fully manifest to me. [UtSst 4.9]

body.translated_text: Whether everything other than this exists as a real thing or not — by great

body.text: svecchayaiva bhagavan nijamārge kāritaḥ padam ahaṃ prabhunaiva &

children.text: tat kathaṃ janavad eva carāmi tvatpadocitam avaimi na kiṃ cit // UtSst_4.10 //
children.translated_text: then how is it that I wander about like ordinary people? I know nothing that befits your feet. [UtSst 4.10]

body.translated_text: By your own will alone, O Lord, I have been made to take a step on your own path by the Master himself;

body.text: ko 'pi deva hṛdi teṣu tāvako jṛmbhate subhagabhāva uttamaḥ &

children.text: tvatkathāmbudaninādacātakā yena te 'pi subhagīkṛtāś ciram // UtSst_4.11 //
children.translated_text: expands — they are like <s>cātaka</s> birds to the thundering cloud of tales about you, by which they too are made blessed for long. [UtSst 4.11]

body.translated_text: O <s>Deva</s> (God), in the hearts of those devotees, a certain supreme and blessed state of yours

body.text: tvajjuṣāṃ tvayi kayāpi līlayā rāga eṣa paripoṣam āgataḥ &

children.text: yad viyogabhuvi saṅkathā tathā saṃsmṛtiḥ phalati saṃgamotsavam // UtSst_4.12 //
children.translated_text: such that in the land of separation, conversation about you, and remembrance, bear the fruit of the festival of union. [UtSst 4.12]

body.translated_text: For those devoted to you, this love for you has been nourished through some divine play,

children.text: śabda āviśati tiryagāśayeṣv apy ayaṃ navanavaprayojanaḥ // UtSst_4.13 //
children.translated_text: enters even into the minds of animals, ever producing fresh and new purposes. [UtSst 4.13]

body.translated_text: This word '<s>Śaṅkara</s>,' nourished by the sprinkling of manifold <s>rasa</s>s (aesthetic sentiments), uttered hundreds of times,

body.text: te jayanti mukhamaṇḍale bhraman asti yeṣu niyataṃ śivadhvaniḥ &

children.text: yaḥ śāśīva prasṛto 'mṛtāśayāt svādu saṃsravati cāmṛtaṃ param // UtSst_4.14 //
children.translated_text: which, spreading like moonlight from a reservoir of nectar, sweetly exudes supreme nectar. [UtSst 4.14]

body.translated_text: Victorious are those in whose mouth-sphere the sound of '<s>Śiva</s>' constantly wanders;

body.text: parisamāptam ivogram idaṃ jagad vigalito 'viralo manaso malaḥ &

children.text: tad api nāsti bhavatpurārgalakavāṭavighaṭṭanam aṇva pi // UtSst_4.15 //
children.translated_text: and yet there is not even the slightest opening of the bolt and door of your city. [UtSst 4.15]

body.translated_text: It is as though this terrible world has come to an end; the dense impurity of the mind has dissolved;

children.text: kim api tat kuru nātha manāg iva sphurasi yena mamābhimukhasthitiḥ // UtSst_4.16 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, do something, even slightly, by which you flash forth facing me. [UtSst 4.16]

body.translated_text: For one whose mind is eager to behold the interior of the ever-blossoming lotus of your face,

body.text: tvadavibhedamater aparaṃ nu kiṃ sukham ihāsti vibhūtir athāparā &

children.text: tad iha tāvakadāsajanasya kiṃ kupatham eti manaḥ parihṛtya tām // UtSst_4.17 //
children.translated_text: Then why does the mind of your servant-folk go astray, abandoning that? [UtSst 4.17]

body.translated_text: What other happiness is there here than the awareness of non-difference from you? Or what other power?

body.text: kṣaṇam apīha na tāvakadāsatāṃ prati bhaveyam ahaṃ kila bhājanam &

children.text: bhavadabhedarasāsavam ādarād avirataṃ rasayeyam ahaṃ na cet // UtSst_4.18 //
children.translated_text: if I did not ceaselessly savor with reverence the wine of the <s>rasa</s> (bliss) of non-difference from you. [UtSst 4.18]

body.translated_text: I would not be a fitting vessel for being your servant even for a moment,

body.text: na kila paśyati satyam ayaṃ janas tava vapur dvayadṛṣṭimalīmasaḥ &

children.text: tad api sarvavidāśritavatsalaḥ kim idam āraṭitaṃ na śṛṇoṣi me // UtSst_4.19 //
children.translated_text: yet, O all-knowing one, affectionate toward those who take refuge, why do you not hear this cry of mine? [UtSst 4.19]

body.translated_text: Indeed, this world does not see your true form, being tainted by the vision of duality;

body.text: smarasi nātha kadācid apīhitaṃ viṣayasaukhyam athāpi mayārthitam &

children.text: satatam eva bhavadvapurīkṣaṇāmṛtamabhīṣṭamalaṃ mama dehi tat // UtSst_4.20 //
children.translated_text: I desire always only the nectar of beholding your form — give me that which is sufficient and desired. [UtSst 4.20]

body.translated_text: Do you remember, O Lord, any deed of mine or any sensory pleasure I ever sought?

body.text: kila yadaiva śivādhvani tāvake kṛtapado 'smi maheśa tavecchayā &

children.text: śubhaśatānyuditāni tadaiva me kim aparaṃ mṛgaye bhavataḥ prabho // UtSst_4.21 //
children.translated_text: hundreds of auspicious things arose for me; what more do I seek from you, O Master? [UtSst 4.21]

body.translated_text: Indeed, from the very moment I set foot on your auspicious path by your will, O <s>Maheśa</s> (Great Lord),

body.text: yatra so 'stam ayam eti vivasvāṃś candramaḥ prabhṛtibhiḥ saha sarvaiḥ &

children.text: kāpi sā vijayate śivarātriḥ svaprabhāprasarabhāsvararūpā // UtSst_4.22 //
children.translated_text: that glorious <s>Śivarātri</s> (Night of Śiva) triumphs, resplendent with the radiance of its own light. [UtSst 4.22]

body.translated_text: Where this sun sets along with the moon and all the rest,

body.text: apy upārjitam ahaṃ triṣu lokeṣv adhipatyam amareśvara manye &

children.translated_text: devoid of essence — all of it bereft of the nectar-taste of touching your feet. [UtSst 4.23]

body.translated_text: Even if I had acquired sovereignty over the three worlds, O Lord of the immortals, I would consider it

children.translated_text: for this bond, even as I bow before you, does not loosen even in the slightest. [UtSst 4.24]

body.translated_text: Alas, O Lord, this firm bondage of the self, consisting of ignorance of you, is fashioned by you yourself,

body.text: mahatām amareśa pūjyamāno 'py aniśaṃ tiṣṭhasi pūjakaikarūpaḥ &

children.translated_text: being seen both externally and internally, you always shine forth as the very body of the seer. [UtSst 4.25]

body.translated_text: Even while being worshipped by the great ones, O Lord of the immortals, you ever remain one with your worshippers;
The fifth hymn, named 'Declaration of One's Own Strength.'

children.text: galepādikayā nātha māṃ svaveśma praveśaya // UtSst_5.1 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, lead me into your own abode, dragging me by the scruff of the neck and feet. [UtSst 5.1]

body.translated_text: Devoted to the enjoyment of mere contact with the lotus of your feet,

children.text: apārarabhasārabdhanartanaḥ syām ahaṃ kadā // UtSst_5.2 //
children.translated_text: when shall I be engaged in a dance begun with unbounded fervor? [UtSst 5.2]

body.translated_text: With my hair colored by the line of dust from the lotus of your feet,

body.text: tvad ekanātho bhagavann iyad evārthaye sadā &

body.translated_text: Having you alone as my lord, O Blessed One, I always pray for just this much:

body.text: aho sudhānidhe svāminn aho mṛṣṭa trilocana &

children.translated_text: O delightful one, O <s>Virūpākṣa</s> (Odd-eyed One)!" — thus may I dance about, crying out. [UtSst 5.4]

body.translated_text: "O treasury of nectar, O Master! O exquisite one, O <s>Trilocana</s> (Three-eyed One)!

children.text: vijṛmbheyabhavadbhaktimadirāmadaghūrṇitaḥ // UtSst_5.5 //
children.translated_text: may I yawn and sway, intoxicated by the wine of devotion to you. [UtSst 5.5]

body.translated_text: With eyes half-closed from the touch of the lotus of your feet,

body.text: cittabhūbhṛd bhuvi vibho vaseyaṃ kvāpi yatra sā &

children.text: nirantaratvatpralāpamayī vṛttir mahārasā // UtSst_5.6 //
children.translated_text: activity which is of supreme <s>rasa</s> (bliss), consisting entirely of incessant talk of you, prevails. [UtSst 5.6]

body.translated_text: O all-pervading Lord, may I dwell somewhere on the mountain of the mind, where that

body.text: yatra devīsametas tvam āsaudhādā ca gopurāt &

children.text: bahurūpaḥ sthitas tasmin vāstavyaḥ syām ahaṃ pure // UtSst_5.7 //
children.translated_text: in many forms — in that city may I be a resident. [UtSst 5.7]

body.translated_text: Where you stand, accompanied by the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), from the palace to the gateway,

children.text: vikasatveṣa yāvan me hṛtpadmaḥ pūjanāya te // UtSst_5.8 //
children.translated_text: so that this heart-lotus of mine may bloom open for your worship. [UtSst 5.8]

body.translated_text: May the rays of your sun blaze forth, O Lord,

body.text: prasīda bhagavan yena tvatpade patitaṃ sadā &

children.text: mano me tattadāsvādya kṣīved iva galed iva // UtSst_5.9 //
children.translated_text: tasting this and that, may become intoxicated as it were, may dissolve as it were. [UtSst 5.9]

body.translated_text: Be gracious, O Lord, so that my mind, forever fallen at your feet,

body.text: praharṣād vātha śokād vā yadi kuṅyād dhaṭād api &

children.text: bāhyād athāntarād bhāvāt prakaṭībhava me prabho // UtSst_5.10 //
children.translated_text: whether from an external or an internal state — become manifest to me, O Master. [UtSst 5.10]

body.translated_text: Whether from joy or from sorrow, whether from a pot or a jar,

body.text: bahir apy antar api tat syandamānaṃ sadāstu me &

children.text: bhavatpādāmbujasparśāmṛtam atyantaśītalam // UtSst_5.11 //
children.translated_text: of touching the lotus of your feet, ever flow within me. [UtSst 5.11]

body.translated_text: Both externally and internally, may that nectar, supremely cool,

children.text: ko 'py eṣa sarvasambhogalaṅghī bhogo 'stu me sadā // UtSst_5.12 //
children.translated_text: may this certain enjoyment, which surpasses all other enjoyments, be mine always. [UtSst 5.12]

body.translated_text: Immersion in the nectar-stream of the nectar of touching your feet —

children.text: ādāya cāmṛtīkṛtya bhuṅkṣva bhaktajanaiḥ samam // UtSst_5.13 //
children.translated_text: and having taken them, transforming them into nectar, enjoy them together with your devotees. [UtSst 5.13]

body.translated_text: Accept, O Lord, the passion and other afflictions offered by me;

children.text: svāmin gṛhāṇa dāseṣu prasādālokanakṣaṇam // UtSst_5.14 //
children.translated_text: bestow upon your servants a moment's glance of grace. [UtSst 5.14]

body.translated_text: O Lord, ever satisfied with the food of all the worlds, resting in comfort,

children.text: namo mahyaṃ śivāyeti pūjayam syāṃ tṛṇāny api // UtSst_5.15 //
children.translated_text: saying 'Homage to myself, who am <s>Śiva</s>,' may I worship even blades of grass. [UtSst 5.15]

body.translated_text: With eyes half-closed from savoring the inner wonder of devotion,

children.text: paśyan bhaktirasābhogair bhaveyam aviyojitaḥ // UtSst_5.16 //
children.translated_text: may I be inseparable from the fullness of the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic bliss) of devotion. [UtSst 5.16]

body.translated_text: Having attained your nature, seeing the world as consisting of the blossoming of my own self,

body.text: ākāmkṣaṇīyam aparaṃ yena nātha na vidyate &

children.text: tava tenādvitīyasya yuktaṃ yat paripūrṇatā // UtSst_5.17 //
children.translated_text: it is fitting that you, the non-dual one, are complete. [UtSst 5.17]

body.translated_text: Since, O Lord, there is nothing else desirable,

children.text: pīyate bhaktipīyūṣarasas tat prāpnuyāṃ padam // UtSst_5.18 //
children.translated_text: where the nectar-essence of the drink of devotion is drunk — may I attain that state. [UtSst 5.18]

body.translated_text: Where there is laughter, where there is dancing, where passion and hatred and the rest are consumed,

children.text: etu mama manasi yāvann aśyatu durvāsanāgandhaḥ // UtSst_5.19 //
children.translated_text: in my mind, until the odor of evil <s>vāsanā</s>s (latent impressions) is consumed. [UtSst 5.19]

body.translated_text: May the fragrance of the flower of contemplation of you, with its ever-novel scent, become firmly established

body.text: kva nu rāgādiṣu rāgaḥ kva ca haracaraṇāmbujeṣu rāgitvam &

children.text: itthaṃ virodharasikaṃ bodhaya hitam amara me hṛdayam // UtSst_5.20 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O immortal one, awaken my heart which delights in such contradiction to what is beneficial. [UtSst 5.20]

body.translated_text: Where indeed is attachment to passions and the like, and where is the state of being attached to the lotus feet of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva)?

children.text: tvaccintāmadirāmadataralīkṛtahṛdaya eva syām // UtSst_5.21 //
children.translated_text: may my heart be ever made restless by intoxication from the wine of contemplation of you. [UtSst 5.21]

body.translated_text: Even while moving through the stages of <s>yoga</s>, even while being turned away from sense objects,

children.text: sarvatra sarvadā me puraḥsaro bhavatu bhaktirasaḥ // UtSst_5.22 //
children.translated_text: everywhere and always, may the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of devotion be my forerunner. [UtSst 5.22]

body.translated_text: In speech, in mind, in intellect, in bodily actions fashioned by the senses —

body.text: śivaśivaśiveti nāmani tava niravadhi nātha japyamāne 'smin &

children.text: āsvādayan bhaveyaṃ kam api mahārasam apunaruktam // UtSst_5.23 //
children.translated_text: may I savor some great <s>rasa</s> (bliss) that is ever unrepeated. [UtSst 5.23]

body.translated_text: '<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>' — while this name of yours, O Lord, is being recited ceaselessly,

children.text: agaṇitāparacinmayagaṇḍike pravicareyam ahaṃ bhavato 'rcitā // UtSst_5.24 //
children.translated_text: in the innumerable orbs of further consciousness — may I roam about, worshipped by you. [UtSst 5.24]

body.translated_text: In the realm of radiant, infinite, pure consciousness, on the path where all inert reality has been absorbed,

body.text: svavapuṣi sphuṭabhāsini śāśvate sthitikṛte na kim apy upayujyate &

children.text: iti matiḥ sudṛḍhā bhavatāt paraṃ mama bhavaccaraṇābjarajaḥ śuceḥ // UtSst_5.25 //
children.translated_text: may this conviction become firmly mine, beyond you, from the pure dust of the lotus of your feet. [UtSst 5.25]

body.translated_text: For the manifestation and sustenance of one's own body that shines forth eternally, nothing whatsoever is needed —

body.text: kim api nātha kadācana cetasi sphurati tad bhavadaṃghritalaspṛśām &

children.text: galati yatra samastamidaṃ sudhāsarasi viśvam idaṃ diśa me sadā // UtSst_5.26 //
children.translated_text: where all this dissolves into a lake of nectar — this entire universe: grant me that always. [UtSst 5.26]

body.translated_text: Something indescribable, O Lord, sometimes flashes in the mind — that which belongs to those who touch the ground of your feet;
The sixth hymn, named 'Manifestation of the Path.'

children.text: nibiḍaṃ tapyamānasya sadā bhūyā dṛśaḥ padam // UtSst_6.1 //
children.translated_text: I who burn intensely — may I always be the object of your gaze. [UtSst 6.1]

body.translated_text: Even for a mere moment, O <s>Īśāna</s> (Lord), separated from you,

children.text: aviyuktaḥ sadaiva syāṃ jagatāpi viyojitaḥ // UtSst_6.2 //
children.translated_text: may I always be unseparated, even if separated from the world. [UtSst 6.2]

body.translated_text: In this <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) whose essence is separation, from you, the beloved Master,

body.text: kāyavāṅmanasair yatra yāmi sarvaṃ tvam eva tat &

children.text: ity eṣa paramārtho 'pi paripūrṇo 'stu me sadā // UtSst_6.3 //
children.translated_text: may this supreme truth be always complete for me. [UtSst 6.3]

body.translated_text: Wherever I go with body, speech, and mind — all of that is you alone;

children.text: bhavatstutikarī bhūyād anurūpaiva vāṅ mama // UtSst_6.4 //
children.translated_text: so may my speech, which praises you, be of a fitting nature. [UtSst 6.4]

body.translated_text: Just as you are free from mental constructs and full of great bliss,

children.text: vicareyaṃ nirākāṅkṣaḥ praharṣaparipūritaḥ // UtSst_6.5 //
children.translated_text: may I wander about, desireless, filled with exhilaration. [UtSst 6.5]

body.translated_text: Through being possessed by you, seeing every state of being as pervaded by you,

children.text: tāvataivāsmi santuṣṭas tato na parikhidyase // UtSst_6.6 //
children.translated_text: I am content with just that much — therefore you need not be troubled. [UtSst 6.6]

body.translated_text: O Lord, may I see the entire world as full of you;

body.text: vilīyamānās tvayy eva vyomni meghalavā iva &

children.text: bhāvā vibhāntu me śaśvat kramanairmalyagāminaḥ // UtSst_6.7 //
children.translated_text: may my mental states forever shine forth, progressing gradually toward purity. [UtSst 6.7]

body.translated_text: Dissolving into you alone, like wisps of cloud dissolving in the sky,

children.text: santataṃ bhātu me ko 'pi bhavamadhyād bhavanmaṇiḥ // UtSst_6.8 //
children.translated_text: may a certain gem of yours ever shine forth for me from within the realm of existence. [UtSst 6.8]

body.translated_text: Having destroyed the unbroken succession of limitless darkness through the spreading of its own radiance,

body.text: kāṃ bhūmikāṃ nādhiśeṣe kiṃ tat syād yan na te vapuḥ &

children.text: śrāntas tenāprayāsena sarvatas tvām avāpnuyām // UtSst_6.9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, wearied by effort, may I attain you everywhere effortlessly. [UtSst 6.9]

body.translated_text: What plane do you not preside over? What is there that is not your body?

children.text: ghaṭatām iyati prāpte kiṃ nātha na jitaṃ mayā // UtSst_6.10 //
children.translated_text: having attained so much, O Lord, what have I not conquered? [UtSst 6.10]

body.translated_text: May the enjoyment of embracing your body be mine by your will alone;

children.text: kurmas te nātha tāmyantas tvām eva mṛgayāmahe // UtSst_6.11 //
children.translated_text: languishing, O Lord, we seek you alone. [UtSst 6.11]

body.translated_text: Become manifest! We do not dishonor you with other prayers;
The seventh hymn, named 'Conquest of Distress.'

body.text: tvayy ānandasarasvati samarasatām etya nātha mama cetaḥ &

children.text: pariharatu sakṛd iyantaṃ bhedādhīnaṃ mahānartham // UtSst_7.1 //
children.translated_text: abandon once and for all this great calamity that depends on duality. [UtSst 7.1]

body.translated_text: O Lord, may my mind, having attained oneness of <s>rasa</s> (essence) with you, the river of bliss,

body.text: etan mama na tv idam iti rāgadveṣādinigaḍadṛḍhamūle &

children.text: nātha bhavanmayataikyapratyayaparaśuḥ patatvantaḥ // UtSst_7.2 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, may the axe of the realization of unity with your nature fall within. [UtSst 7.2]

body.translated_text: 'This is mine but not that' — in this conviction, firmly rooted through the fetters of passion, hatred, and the rest,

children.text: bhagavann ānandarasaplutāstu me cinmayī mūrtiḥ // UtSst_7.3 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, may my form, consisting of pure consciousness, be flooded with the <s>rasa</s> (bliss) of joy. [UtSst 7.3]

body.translated_text: May the chain of stains of mental constructs dissolve; may unbounded freedom surge forth in the heart;

children.text: āpyāyayatu rasair māṃ pravṛddhapakṣo yathā bhavāmi khagaḥ // UtSst_7.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>rasa</s>s (essences), nourish me until I become a bird with fully grown wings. [UtSst 7.4]

body.translated_text: Like a bird rolling in the egg-shell of existence made of passion and the rest, may the mother-bird of devotion to you, with those very

children.text: cittam idaṃ niḥśeṣitaviṣayaviṣāsaṅgavāsanāvadhi me // UtSst_7.5 //
children.translated_text: to the point where the latent impressions of attachment to the poison of sense-objects are completely exhausted. [UtSst 7.5]

body.translated_text: May this mind of mine attain skill in savoring the essential <s>rasa</s> (taste) of the nectar of contemplation of your feet,

children.text: cetomaṇir vimūñcaturāgādikataptavahnikaṇān // UtSst_7.6 //
children.translated_text: may this mind-jewel of mine cast off far away the sparks of the fire kindled by passion and the rest. [UtSst 7.6]

body.translated_text: Through the touch of the rays of the sun of devotion to you,

body.text: tasmin pade bhavantaṃ satatam upaślokayeyam atyuccaiḥ &

children.text: hariharyaśvaviriñcā api yatra bahiḥ pratīkṣante // UtSst_7.7 //
children.translated_text: where even <s>Hari</s>, <s>Haryaśva</s> (Indra), and <s>Viriñca</s> (Brahmā) wait outside. [UtSst 7.7]

body.translated_text: In that state, may I hymn you constantly and most loudly,

children.text: śivamayam akhilaṃ lokaṃ kriyāś ca pūjāmayī sakalāḥ // UtSst_7.8 //
children.translated_text: the entire world as pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>, and all actions as consisting of worship. [UtSst 7.8]

body.translated_text: Through the bewilderment born of the intoxication of devotion, may I see with all my faculties, in full,

children.text: sūtvā subaddhamūlā mameti buddhiṃ dṛḍhīkurutām // UtSst_7.9 //
children.translated_text: become firmly rooted and strengthen the conviction 'she is mine.' [UtSst 7.9]

body.translated_text: May the bride of devotion to you, embraced by my mind, having given birth to children such as <s>aṇimā</s> (the power of becoming minute) and the rest,
The eighth hymn, named 'Extraordinary Strengthening.'

body.text: yaḥ prasādalava īśvarasthito yā ca bhaktir iva mām upeyuṣī &

children.text: tau parasparasamanvitau kadā tādṛśe vapuṣi rūḍhim eṣyataḥ // UtSst_8.1 //
children.translated_text: when will those two, united with each other, attain maturity in such a form? [UtSst 8.1]

body.translated_text: That particle of grace residing in you, O Lord, and that devotion which has, as it were, come to me —

children.text: sarvakālam iha me param astu jñānayogamahimādi vidūre // UtSst_8.2 //
children.translated_text: may I have that supreme thing always here — let the glory of <s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) and the rest remain far away. [UtSst 8.2]

body.translated_text: May a certain satisfaction-<s>rasa</s> (bliss of contentment), born of serving your lordship, arise within;

body.text: lokavadbhavatu me viṣayeṣu sphīta eva bhagavanparitarṣaḥ &

children.text: kevalaṃ tava śarīratayaitān+ lokayeyam aham astavikalpaḥ // UtSst_8.3 //
children.translated_text: only let me regard them as your body — I who am free from mental constructs. [UtSst 8.3]

body.translated_text: O Lord, let my thirst for sense objects be abundant, just as it is for ordinary people;

body.text: dehabhūmiṣu tathā manasi tvaṃ prāṇavartmani ca bhedam upete &

children.text: saṃvidaḥ pathiṣu teṣu ca tena svātmanā mama bhava sphuṭarūpaḥ // UtSst_8.4 //
children.translated_text: and on those paths of consciousness — through your own self, become clearly manifest to me. [UtSst 8.4]

body.translated_text: In the planes of the body, in the mind, on the path of the breath, assuming differentiation,

body.text: nijanijeṣu padeṣu patantv imāḥ karaṇavṛttaya ullasitā mama &

children.text: kṣaṇamapīśa manāg api maiva bhūt tvadavibhedarasakṣatisāhasam // UtSst_8.5 //
children.translated_text: but even for a moment, O Lord, even slightly, may there never be the violence of losing the <s>rasa</s> (bliss) of non-difference from you. [UtSst 8.5]

body.translated_text: Let these exuberant activities of my senses fall upon their respective objects;

children.text: vapur akhilapadārthapaddhater vyavahārān ativartayeya tān // UtSst_8.6 //
children.translated_text: may I transcend the conventions of the entire course of worldly objects. [UtSst 8.6]

body.translated_text: Through the power of being possessed by you, experiencing the body as light, smooth, white, transparent, and cool,

body.text: vikasatu svavapur bhavadātmakaṃ samupayāntu jaganti mamāṅgatām &

children.text: vrajatu sarvam idaṃ dvayavalgitaṃ smṛtipathopagame 'py anupākhyatām // UtSst_8.7 //
children.translated_text: may all this play of duality pass into unnamability when it enters the path of recollection. [UtSst 8.7]

body.translated_text: May my own body, having your nature, blossom forth; may the worlds attain the status of my limbs;

children.text: mama ghaṭeta yathā bhavadadvayāprathanaghoradarīparipūraṇam // UtSst_8.8 //
children.translated_text: so that the filling of the terrible cave of the realization of non-duality with you may be accomplished for me. [UtSst 8.8]

body.translated_text: May there also arise such a flood of supreme nectar, O Lord, in your forest — behold! —

children.text: sakalalokasukheṣu parāṅmukho na bhavitāsmy ubhayacyuta eva kim // UtSst_8.9 //
children.translated_text: I will become indifferent to all the pleasures of the world — or will I remain fallen from both? // UtSst 8.9 //

body.translated_text: Will there ever be a time when, through the slightest sprinkling of even a drop of nectar of union with You,

body.text: satatam eva bhavaccaraṇāmbujākaracarasya hi haṃsavarasya me &

children.text: upari mūlatalād api cāntarād upanamatv aja bhaktimṛṇālikā // UtSst_8.10 //
children.translated_text: May the lotus-stalk of devotion bow down from above, from the root, and from within, O Unborn One! // UtSst 8.10 //

body.translated_text: For me, who am like the best of swans whose activity is at the lake of Your lotus-feet,

body.text: upayāntu vibho samastavastūny api cintāviṣayaṃ dṛśaḥ padaṃ ca &

children.text: mama darśanacintanaprakāśāmṛtasārāṇi paraṃ parisphurantu // UtSst_8.11 //
children.translated_text: And may they shine forth supremely, their essence being the nectar of the light of seeing and contemplating // UtSst 8.11 //

body.translated_text: O all-pervading Lord, may all things come within the range of thought and the domain of vision,

body.text: parameśvara teṣu teṣu kṛcchreṣv api nāmopanamatsv ahaṃ bhaveyam &

children.text: na paraṃ gatabhīs tvadaṅgasaṅgādupajātādhikasammado 'pi yāvat // UtSst_8.12 //
children.translated_text: Not merely fearless through contact with Your body, but one in whom supreme joy has arisen // UtSst 8.12 //

body.translated_text: O Supreme Lord, even in various difficulties, may I become one who bows to [Your] name —

body.text: bhavadātmani viśvam umbhitaṃ yad bhavataivāpi bahiḥ prakāśyate tat &

children.text: iti yad dṛḍhaniścayopajuṣṭaṃ tad idāniṃ sphuṭam eva bhāsatām // UtSst_8.13 //
children.translated_text: May this, endowed with firm conviction, now shine forth clearly // UtSst 8.13 //

body.translated_text: That the universe is contained in Your nature, and that it is also manifested externally by You —
The ninth hymn called 'Victory of Freedom' (<s>Svātantryavijaya</s>).

children.text: pravarteta vihāyānyan mama tvatsparśane manaḥ // UtSst_9.1 //
children.translated_text: Moistened with the fresh nine <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), engage in the touch of You? // UtSst 9.1 //

body.translated_text: When will my mind, abandoning everything else, eager for the tasting of enjoyment

children.text: kadā sākṣātkariṣyāmi bhavantam ayam utsukaḥ // UtSst_9.2 //
children.translated_text: When, eager as I am, will I directly realize You? // UtSst 9.2 //

body.translated_text: Devoted to You alone, possessing the great wealth of merely worshipping Your feet —

children.text: paṭapaṭiti vighaṭitākhilamahārgalas tvām upaiṣyāmi // UtSst_9.3 //
children.translated_text: Will I come to You with all great bolts shattered suddenly with a cracking sound? // UtSst 9.3 //

body.translated_text: When, due to deep love, having become indifferent-minded,

children.text: kadā nātha vaśīkuryāṃ bhavadbhaktiprabhāvataḥ // UtSst_9.4 //
children.translated_text: Bring under control all deities who are established in the essence of one's own consciousness as their heart? // UtSst 9.4 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when shall I, through the power of devotion to You,

body.text: kadā me syād vibho bhūri bhaktyānandarasotsavaḥ &

children.text: yadālokasukhānandī pṛthaṅ nāmāpi lapsyate // UtSst_9.5 //
children.translated_text: [A festival] at whose sight even one who delights in bliss will receive a distinct name? // UtSst 9.5 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when will I have the abundant festival of the bliss-essence of devotion,

body.text: īśvaram abhayam udāraṃ pūrṇam akāraṇam apahnutātmānaṃ &

children.text: sahasābhijñāya kadā svāmijanaṃ lajjayiṣyāmi // UtSst_9.6 //
children.translated_text: And who has concealed Himself — will I put my masters to shame? // UtSst 9.6 //

body.translated_text: When, having suddenly recognized the Lord — fearless, generous, complete, causeless,

body.text: kadā kām api tāṃ nātha tava vallabhatām iyām &

children.text: yayā māṃ prati na kvāpi yuktaṃ te syāt palāyitum // UtSst_9.7 //
children.translated_text: By which it would not be appropriate for You to flee from me anywhere? // UtSst 9.7 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when will I attain that certain belovedness of Yours,

children.text: dṛṣṭyānumoditarasāplāvitaḥ syāṃ kadā vibho // UtSst_9.8 //
children.translated_text: Will I be flooded with the sentiment approved by that vision, O Lord? // UtSst 9.8 //

body.translated_text: When, seeing all beings as having worship of You as their true nature,

body.text: jñānasya paramā bhūmir yogasya paramā daśā &

children.text: tvadbhaktir yā vibho karhi pūrṇa me syāt tadarthitā // UtSst_9.9 //
children.translated_text: When will my desire for that be fulfilled? // UtSst 9.9 //

body.translated_text: Devotion to You, O Lord, which is the highest ground of knowledge and the highest state of yoga —

children.text: tvaccaraṇavaranidhānaṃ sarvasya prakaṭayiṣyāmi // UtSst_9.10 //
children.translated_text: Will I reveal to all the treasure of the boon of Your feet? // UtSst 9.10 //

body.translated_text: When, having suddenly seized [You] firmly, overwhelmed with joy,

children.text: syāṃ yatheśa na kiñcin me māyācchāyābilaṃ bhavet // UtSst_9.11 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, so that nothing in me remains darkened by the shadow of <s>māyā</s>? // UtSst 9.11 //

body.translated_text: When will I become filled with the pure light of Your vision spreading in all directions,

children.text: kadā bhaveyaṃ bhagavaṃs tvadbhaktagaṇanāyakaḥ // UtSst_9.12 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, when will I become the leader of the host of Your devotees? // UtSst 9.12 //

body.translated_text: Having made the entire circle my own, becoming indifferent [to everything else] —

children.text: mahābhimānaḥ karhi syāṃ tvadbhaktirasapūritaḥ // UtSst_9.13 //
children.translated_text: When will I, filled with the essence of devotion to You, become the great pride [of the world]? // UtSst 9.13 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, You are the unprecedented foundation of the world's self-esteem;

children.text: śayīyam iva śītāṅghrikuśeśayayuge kadā // UtSst_9.14 //
children.translated_text: When will I lie as if resting on the pair of Your cool lotus-feet? // UtSst 9.14 //

body.translated_text: Well-established in the embrace of the glory devoid of all objects,

children.text: kadā pāraṃ gamiṣyāmi bhaviṣyāmi kadā kṛtī // UtSst_9.15 //
children.translated_text: Enriched by the wine of devotion? When will I become accomplished? // UtSst 9.15 //

body.translated_text: When will I reach the far shore of the wealth of enjoyment of worshipping You,

children.text: hāsollāsitavadanas tvatsparśarasaṃ kadāpsyāmi // UtSst_9.16 //
children.translated_text: Face lit up with laughter — when will I obtain the taste of Your touch? // UtSst 9.16 //

body.translated_text: With tears of bliss flowing, speech faltering and wandering, stammering with choked sobbing,

body.text: paśujanasamānavṛttām avadhūya daśām imāṃ kadā śambho &

children.text: āsvādayeya tāvakabhaktocitam ātmano rūpam // UtSst_9.17 //
children.translated_text: Will I savor the form of my Self appropriate for Your devotee? // UtSst 9.17 //

body.translated_text: O <s>Śambhu</s>, when, having shaken off this condition that resembles the behavior of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>),

children.text: tvadbhaktirasāyanapānakriḍhāniṣṭaḥ kadāsīya // UtSst_9.18 //
children.translated_text: When will I be content in the play of drinking the elixir of devotion to You? // UtSst 9.18 //

body.translated_text: Having obtained <s>siddhis</s> (powers) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>, with all distress and fear dissolved,

body.text: nātha kadā sa tathāvidha ākrando me samuccared vāci &

children.text: yat samanantaram eva sphurati puras tāvakī mūrtiḥ // UtSst_9.19 //
children.translated_text: That immediately thereafter Your form flashes forth before me? // UtSst 9.19 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when will such a cry arise in my speech

children.text: vastv avastv idam ayatnata eva tvāṃ kadā samavalokayitāsmi // UtSst_9.20 //
children.translated_text: Whether this [world] be real or unreal — when will I effortlessly behold You? // UtSst 9.20 //

body.translated_text: With my mind intent on the passion of embracing Your lotus-feet ever more deeply,
The tenth hymn called 'Unbroken Stream' (<s>Avicchedabhaṅga</s>).

body.text: na soḍhavyam avaśyam te jagadekaprabhor idam &

children.text: māheśvarāś ca lokānām itareṣāṃ samāś ca yat // UtSst_10.1 //
children.translated_text: That Your <s>Māheśvaras</s> are equal to other people // UtSst 10.1 //

body.translated_text: This should certainly not be tolerated by You, the sole ruler of the world —

children.text: yatra tatra gatā bhogāṃs te kāṃś cid upabhuñjate // UtSst_10.2 //
children.translated_text: Wherever they go, they enjoy some pleasures // UtSst 10.2 //

body.translated_text: Those who always follow Your feet with love,

body.text: bhartā kālāntako yatra bhavāṃs tatra kuto rujaḥ &

children.text: tatra cetarabhogāśā kā lakṣmīr yatra tāvakī // UtSst_10.3 //
children.translated_text: And where Your glory is present, what hope for other enjoyments can there be? // UtSst 10.3 //

body.translated_text: Where You are the protector, the Ender of Time — whence can there be pain?

children.text: tadaiva sarvaḥ kālo 'sya tvadānandena pūryate // UtSst_10.4 //
children.translated_text: At that very instant all of his time is filled with Your bliss // UtSst 10.4 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, by whatever momentary happiness You are obtained,

children.text: sūryas tathā te prasṛtaḥ saṃhārī tejasaḥ kaṇaḥ // UtSst_10.5 //
children.translated_text: The sun likewise is a particle of Your destructive radiance spread forth // UtSst 10.5 //

body.translated_text: The moon is a drop of Your bliss-nectar fallen to earth;

body.text: baliṃ yāmas tṛtīyāya netrāyāsmai tava prabho &

children.text: alaukikasya kasyāpi māhātmyasyaikalakṣmaṇe // UtSst_10.6 //
children.translated_text: The sole mark of some extraordinary greatness // UtSst 10.6 //

body.translated_text: We offer tribute to this third eye of Yours, O Lord —

children.text: kathañcid yasya vā harṣaḥ ko 'pi tena tvam īkṣitaḥ // UtSst_10.7 //
children.translated_text: Or whoever has some inexplicable joy — by that [eye] You have been seen // UtSst 10.7 //

body.translated_text: One who greatly rejoices at the sight of You — he has indeed been [first] seen by that [third eye];

body.text: yeṣām prasanno 'si vibho yair labdhaṃ hṛdayaṃ tava &

children.text: ākṛṣya tvatpurāttais tu bāhyam ābhyantarīkṛtam // UtSst_10.8 //
children.translated_text: By them, having drawn from Your city, what was external has been made internal // UtSst 10.8 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, those with whom You are pleased, who have won Your heart —

body.text: tvad ṛte nikhilaṃ viśvaṃ samadṛgyātam īkṣyatām &

children.text: īśvaraḥ punar etasya tvam eko viṣamekṣaṇaḥ // UtSst_10.9 //
children.translated_text: But You, O Lord, are the one with unequal vision (<s>viṣamekṣaṇa</s>) over this [world] // UtSst 10.9 //

body.translated_text: Without You, let the entire universe be viewed with equal vision;

body.text: āstāṃ bhavatprabhāveṇa vinā sattaiva nāsti yat &

children.text: tvaddūṣaṇakathā yeṣām tvad ṛte nopapadyate // UtSst_10.10 //
children.translated_text: Even those who speak ill of You cannot do so without [Your power] // UtSst 10.10 //

body.translated_text: Leave aside [the argument] that without Your power nothing even exists —

children.text: tvayi cet syān mama vibho kim anyad upayujyate // UtSst_10.11 //
children.translated_text: Were to be established in You — what else would be needed? // UtSst 10.11 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, if my mind, free from all external and internal obstacles,

children.text: anye bhramanti bhagavann ātmany evātisusthitāḥ // UtSst_10.12 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, others wander about, greatly established in their very Self // UtSst 10.12 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, some wander about, greatly distressed in their very Self;

children.text: tvām īśa tvatsamācāramātrāt siddhyanti jantavaḥ // UtSst_10.13 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, beings attain perfection merely from imitating Your conduct // UtSst 10.13 //

body.translated_text: Even without drinking the nectar of devotion to You and without seeing You,

body.text: bhṛtyā vayaṃ tava vibho tena trijagatāṃ yathā &

children.text: bibharṣy ātmānam evaṃ te bharttavyā vayam apy alam // UtSst_10.14 //
children.translated_text: So You must sustain us as well — this is entirely fitting // UtSst 10.14 //

body.translated_text: We are Your servants, O Lord; therefore, just as You sustain the three worlds,

children.text: tvayi sparśarase 'tyantatarasutkaṇṭhito(?) 'smi te // UtSst_10.15 //
children.translated_text: I remain extremely eager for the taste of Your touch // UtSst 10.15 //

body.translated_text: Even having seen You, the Self of the world, consisting of supreme bliss and nectar,

body.text: deva duḥkhāny aśeṣāṇi yāni saṃsāriṇām api &

children.text: ghṛtyākhyabhavadīyātmayutāny āyānti sahyatām // UtSst_10.16 //
children.translated_text: When united with Your Self called compassion, become bearable // UtSst 10.16 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, even all the sufferings of those in <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text: sarvajñe sarvaśaktau ca tvayy eva sati cinmaye &

children.text: sarvathāpy asato nātha yuktāsya jagataḥ prathā // UtSst_10.17 //
children.translated_text: The manifestation of this non-existent world is appropriate in every way // UtSst 10.17 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when You, the all-knowing, all-powerful, and consciousness-embodied, alone exist,

children.text: nṛtyanti pavanoddhūtāḥ kārpāsāḥ picavo yathā // UtSst_10.18 //
children.translated_text: They dance like cotton fibers blown by the wind // UtSst 10.18 //

body.translated_text: These qualities, enlivened by You, flash forth even though they are like clods of earth —

body.text: yadi nātha guṇeṣv ātmābhimāno na bhavet tataḥ &

children.text: kena hīyeta jagatas tvadekātmatayā prathā // UtSst_10.19 //
children.translated_text: Then by what would the world's manifestation as having You alone as its essence be diminished? // UtSst 10.19 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, if there were no self-identification with qualities,

children.text: tvatkopapāvakasparśapūtā ye parameśvara // UtSst_10.20 //
children.translated_text: Those purified by the touch of the fire of Your anger, O Supreme Lord // UtSst 10.20 //

body.translated_text: Even those great ones who are worthy of Your veneration, who have undergone dissolution, are [still] venerable —

children.text: sarvato 'pīśa tat kasmāt tamasi prasarāmy aham // UtSst_10.21 //
children.translated_text: Everywhere — then why do I spread into darkness? // UtSst 10.21 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when Your great luminous form is clearly present and established,

body.text: avibhāgo bhavān eva svarūpam amṛtaṃ mama &

children.text: tathāpi martyadharmāṇām aham evaikam āspadam // UtSst_10.22 //
children.translated_text: Yet I alone am the sole abode of mortal conditions // UtSst 10.22 //

body.translated_text: You alone, undivided, are my immortal nature;

children.text: praṇāmāṅkaś ca śirasi sa evaikaḥ prabhāvitaḥ // UtSst_10.23 //
children.translated_text: Of the name '<s>Maheśvara</s>' and the mark of prostration on his head // UtSst 10.23 //

body.translated_text: He alone is truly empowered who has the verbal ornament

body.text: sadasac ca bhavān eva yena tenāprayāsataḥ &

children.text: svarasenaiva bhagavaṃs tathā siddhiḥ kathaṃ na me // UtSst_10.24 //
children.translated_text: Spontaneously, O Lord — how can perfection not be mine? // UtSst 10.24 //

body.translated_text: You alone are both the existent and the non-existent; therefore, effortlessly,

body.text: śivadāsaḥ śivaikātmā kiṃ yan nāsādayet sukham &

children.text: tarpyo 'smi devamukhyānām api yenāmṛtāsavaiḥ // UtSst_10.25 //
children.translated_text: By which I should be satisfied even with the nectar-wines of the chief gods? // UtSst 10.25 //

body.translated_text: What happiness would a servant of <s>Śiva</s>, one with <s>Śiva</s> in essence, not attain —

children.text: grasase tvaṃ mahāvahniḥ sarvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam // UtSst_10.26 //
children.translated_text: You, the great fire having the form of bile, consume everything, moving and unmoving // UtSst 10.26 //

body.translated_text: Situated in the space between the heart and the navel of living beings,
The eleventh hymn called 'Breathing of Eagerness' (<s>Autsukyaviśvasita</s>).

body.text: jagad idam athavā suhṛdo bandhujano vā na bhavati mama kim api &

children.text: tvaṃ punar etat sarvaṃ yadā tadā ko 'paro me 'stu // UtSst_11.1 //
children.translated_text: But when You are all this, then what other [concern] can there be for me? // UtSst 11.1 //

body.translated_text: Whether this world, or friends, or kinfolk — nothing is mine;

body.text: svāmin maheśvaras tvaṃ sākṣāt sarvaṃ jagat tvam eveti &

children.text: vastv eva siddhim etv iti yācñā tatrāpi yācñaiva // UtSst_11.2 //
children.translated_text: May the reality itself attain fulfillment; the prayer there too is itself but a prayer // UtSst 11.2 //

body.translated_text: O Master, You are <s>Maheśvara</s> directly; the entire universe is You indeed —

body.text: tribhuvanādhipatitvam apīha yat tṛṇam iva pratibhāti bhavajjuṣaḥ &

children.text: kim iva tasya phalaṃ śubhakarmaṇo bhavati nātha bhavatsmaraṇād ṛte // UtSst_11.3 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, what fruit of good deeds can there be other than remembering You? // UtSst 11.3 //

body.translated_text: Even the sovereignty of the three worlds appears like a blade of grass to one devoted to You;

body.text: yena naiva bhavato 'sti vibhinnaṃ kiñcanāpi jagatāṃ prabhavaś ca &

children.text: tvadvijṛmbhitam ato 'dbhutakarmasv apy udeti na tava stutibandhaḥ // UtSst_11.4 //
children.translated_text: Your display of wonder — therefore no hymn of praise arises for You even in wondrous deeds // UtSst 11.4 //

body.translated_text: Since nothing at all is different from You, and You are the origin of all worlds —

body.text: tvanmayo 'smi bhavadarcananiṣṭhaḥ sarvadāham iti cāpy avirāmam &

children.text: bhāvayann api vibho svarasena svapnago 'pi na tathā kim iva syām // UtSst_11.5 //
children.translated_text: I am not even like that in a dream — what indeed can I be? // UtSst 11.5 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, even though I contemplate continuously and spontaneously that 'I am filled with You, I am always established in worshipping You,'

children.text: teṣu visram iva bhavati samastaṃ bhogajātam amarair api mṛgyam // UtSst_11.6 //
children.translated_text: All enjoyment — even that sought by the gods — becomes like a foul smell // UtSst 11.6 //

body.translated_text: For those who are slightly touched by even a trace of the fragrance arising from Your lotus-feet,

body.text: hṛdi te na tu vidyate 'nyad anyad vacane karmaṇi cānyad eva śaṃbho &

children.text: paramārthasato 'py anugraho vā yadi vā nigraha eka eva kāryaḥ // UtSst_11.7 //
children.translated_text: Either grace or punishment alone should be enacted, even toward the ultimately real // UtSst 11.7 //

body.translated_text: In Your heart there is one thing, in Your speech another, and in Your action something else, O <s>Śambhu</s> —

children.text: śambho tathā kalaya śīghram upaimi yena sarvottamāṃ dhuram apojjhitaduḥkhamārgaḥ // UtSst_11.8 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Śambhu</s>, arrange it quickly so that I attain the highest station, having abandoned the path of suffering // UtSst 11.8 //

body.translated_text: I am deluded, I am afflicted by suffering, I am afraid of old age and other defects, I am devoid of power, I am devoted to You —

body.text: tvatkarṇadeśama dhiśayya mahārghabhāvam ākranditāni mama tucchatarāṇi yānti &

children.text: vaṃśāntarālapatitāni jalaikadeśakhaṇḍāni mauktikamaṇitvam ivodvahanti // UtSst_11.9 //
children.translated_text: Just as water-drops falling into the hollow of a bamboo assume the state of pearl-gems // UtSst 11.9 //

body.translated_text: My cries, most trivial, falling near Your ear, attain the state of great value —

body.text: kim iva ca labhyate bata na tair api nātha janaiḥ kṣaṇam api kaitavād api ca ye tava nāmni ratāḥ &

children.text: śiśiramayūkhaśekhara tathā kuru yena mama kṣatamaraṇo 'ṇimādikam upaimi yathā vibhavam // UtSst_11.10 //
children.translated_text: O Moon-crested One, act so that I, with death destroyed, attain powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> and such glory // UtSst 11.10 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, what indeed is not obtained even by those who, even for a moment, even through deceit, delight in Your name?

body.text: śambho śarva śaśaṅkaśekhara śiva tryakṣākṣamālādhara śrīmann ugrakapālalāñchana lasadbhīmatriśūlāyudha &

children.text: kāruṇyāmbunidhe trilokaracanāśīlograśaktyātmaka śrīkaṇṭhāśu vināśayāśubhabharān ādhat svasiddhiṃ parām // UtSst_11.11 //
children.translated_text: Ocean of compassion, whose fierce power-nature is engaged in creating the three worlds — O <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, quickly destroy the burden of inauspiciousness and bestow supreme attainment! // UtSst 11.11 //

body.translated_text: O <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, Moon-crested <s>Śiva</s>, three-eyed one bearing the rosary, glorious one marked with the terrible skull, shining with the fearsome trident-weapon,

body.text: tat kiṃ nātha bhaven na yatra bhagavān nirmātṛtām aśnute bhāvaḥ syāt kim u tasya cetanavato nāśāsti yaṃ śaṅkaraḥ &

children.text: itthaṃ te parameśvarākṣatamahāśakteḥ sadā saṃśritaḥ saṃsāre 'tra nirantarādhividhuraḥ kliśyāmy ahaṃ kevalam // UtSst_11.12 //
children.translated_text: Thus, always taking refuge in Your undiminished great power, O Supreme Lord, I suffer merely, constantly afflicted in this <s>saṃsāra</s> // UtSst 11.12 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, what cannot come into being where the Lord exercises creatorship? Can that conscious being who is <s>Śaṅkara</s> ever be destroyed?

body.text: yady apy atra varapradoddhatatamāḥ pīḍājarāmṛtyava ete vā kṣaṇam āsatāṃ bahumataḥ śabdādir evāsthiraḥ &

children.text: tatrāpi spṛhayāmi santatasukhākāṅkṣī ciraṃ sthāsnave bhogāsvādayutatvadaṅghrikamaladhyānāgrya jīvātave // UtSst_11.13 //
children.translated_text: Even so, longing for perpetual happiness, I desire something enduring and life-giving: the supreme meditation on Your lotus-feet united with the tasting of enjoyments // UtSst 11.13 //

body.translated_text: Even though in this [world] afflictions, old age, and death are the most prominent gifts [of existence] — or let these be for just a moment; even the unstable [pleasures] beginning with sound are esteemed —

body.text: he nātha praṇatārtināśanapaṭo śreyonidhe dhūrjaṭe duḥkhaikāyatanasya janmamaraṇatrastasya me sāmpratam &

children.text: tac ceṣṭasva yathā manojñaviṣayāsvādapradā uttamā jīvann eva samaśnuve 'ham acalāḥ siddhīs tvadarcāparaḥ // UtSst_11.14 //
children.translated_text: Now act so that I, devoted to worshipping You, may enjoy while yet living the supreme, unwavering <s>siddhis</s> that grant the tasting of delightful objects // UtSst 11.14 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, skilled in destroying the suffering of those who bow, O treasure of blessings, O <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> — for me, the sole abode of suffering, terrified by birth and death —

children.text: sarvaprakāśātiśayaprakāśāyendulakṣmaṇe // UtSst_11.15 //
children.translated_text: Whose light surpasses the luminosity of all, who bears the mark of the moon // UtSst 11.15 //

body.translated_text: Salutations to the one whose sole function is to destroy the great darkness of delusion,
The twelfth hymn called 'Pointing to the Secret' (<s>Rahasyanirdeśa</s>).

body.text: sahakāri na kiñcid iṣyate bhavato na pratibandhakaṃ dṛṣi &

children.text: bhavataiva hi sarvam āplutaṃ katham adyāpi tathāpi nekṣase // UtSst_12.1 //
children.translated_text: Since everything is pervaded by You — how is it that even now You do not see? // UtSst 12.1 //

body.translated_text: Nothing auxiliary is desired for You, nor is there any obstruction to Your vision;

children.text: prabhavantam api svataḥ sadā paripaśyeyam apoḍhaviśvakam // UtSst_12.2 //
children.translated_text: May I behold the one who arises of himself at all times, who has discarded the universe // UtSst 12.2 //

body.translated_text: Whether from the host of mental states, from the assemblage of senses, or from the midst of awakened awareness —

body.text: kathaṃ te jāyeran katham api ca te darśanapathaṃ vrajeyuḥ kenāpi prakṛtimahatāṅkena khacitaḥ &

children.text: tathotthāyotthāya sthalajalatṛṇāder akhilataḥ padārthadyānsṛṣṭisravadamṛtapūrair(?) vikirasi // UtSst_12.3 //
children.translated_text: Thus, arising again and again from earth, water, grass, and all else, You scatter forth streams of nectar flowing from the meditation on emanation // UtSst 12.3 //

body.translated_text: How can they arise, and how can they also enter the path of Your vision — stamped with some innate, vast mark?

children.text: unmūlitatṛṣo mattā vicaranti yathāruci // UtSst_12.4 //
children.translated_text: With their thirst uprooted, intoxicated, they wander about as they please // UtSst 12.4 //

body.translated_text: Those who have directly realized Your form and are nourished by the nectar flowing [from it],

body.text: na tadā na sadā na caikadety api sā yatra na kāladhīr bhavet &

children.text: tad idaṃ bhavadīyadarśanaṃ na ca nityaṃ na ca kathyate 'nyathā // UtSst_12.5 //
children.translated_text: this vision of Yours is neither called 'eternal' nor called 'otherwise.' //UtSst 12.5//

body.translated_text: Not 'then,' not 'always,' not 'once' — [the vision] where there is no notion of time;

children.text: yad viśeyam abhisandhimātratas tvatsudhāsadanam arcanāya te // UtSst_12.6 //
children.translated_text: that I may enter, merely by intention, Your nectar-abode, to worship You. //UtSst 12.6//

body.translated_text: For me, whose mind is elated at beholding You, may this much yogic attainment be mine always:

children.text: ullasanti vimalāni helayā ceṣṭitāni ca vacāṃsi ca sphuṭam // UtSst_12.7 //
children.translated_text: their actions and their words clearly shine forth, pure and effortless. //UtSst 12.7//

body.translated_text: For the great souls whose minds have blossomed through attaining the thought-free vision of You,

children.text: bhavabhūmiṣu tāsu tāsv ahaṃ prabhum arceyam anargalakriyaḥ // UtSst_12.8 //
children.translated_text: may I, with unrestrained activity, worship the Lord in each of these planes of existence. //UtSst 12.8//

body.translated_text: Dwelling fearlessly within the interior of Your lotus-feet,

children.text: atimātramadhūpayogataḥ paritṛpto vicareyam icchayā // UtSst_12.9 //
children.translated_text: fully satisfied through excessive enjoyment of honey, may I wander about freely. //UtSst 12.9//

body.translated_text: Merged in the interior of the lotus of Your feet, with all seeking for anything else dissolved,

children.text: tasyāpy avaśyam uditaṃ sannidhānaṃ tavocitam // UtSst_12.10 //
children.translated_text: Your gracious presence inevitably manifests — this is fitting for You. //UtSst 12.10//

body.translated_text: Even for one in whom the intention of worshiping You has arisen as if from pretense,

body.text: bhagavann itarān apekṣiṇā nitarām ekarasena cetasā &

children.text: sulabhaṃ sakalopaśāyinaṃ prabhum ātṛpti pibeyam asmi kim // UtSst_12.11 //
children.translated_text: may I drink to my fill of the Lord who is easily accessible and who reposes in all — am I [not worthy]? //UtSst 12.11//

body.translated_text: O Blessed One, with a mind single-flavored, not looking toward others,

body.text: tvayā nirākṛtam sarvaṃ heyam etat tad eva tu &

children.text: tvanmayaṃ samupādeyam ity ayaṃ sārasaṃgrahaḥ // UtSst_12.12 //
children.translated_text: pervaded by You, is to be accepted — this is the essence of the matter. //UtSst 12.12//

body.translated_text: All this that is to be rejected has been rejected by You; and that very same [reality],

children.text: bhavato bahir apy abhāvamātrā katham īśān bhavet samarcyate vā // UtSst_12.13 //
children.translated_text: that which is outside You is mere non-existence — how, O Lord, could it exist or be worshiped? //UtSst 12.13//

body.translated_text: The entire world of entities that moves within You is worshiped precisely because it leads to the Lord;

children.text: kṣobhe 'py adhyakṣamī kṣeyaṃ tryakṣa tvām eva sarvataḥ // UtSst_12.14 //
children.translated_text: even in agitation, O three-eyed one, may I perceive You everywhere as the supreme witness. //UtSst 12.14//

body.translated_text: Soundless, thought-free, without distraction, and unceasing —

body.text: prakaṭaya nijadhāma deva yasmiṃs tvam asi sadā parameśvarīsametaḥ &
