children.text: prabhucaraṇarajaḥsamānakakṣyāḥ kim aviśvāsapadaṃ bhānti bhṛtyāḥ // UtSst_12.15 //
children.translated_text: are not Your servants, who are of the same rank as the dust of the Lord's feet, worthy of trust? //UtSst 12.15//

body.translated_text: Reveal Your own abode, O Lord, where You always dwell together with the Supreme Goddess;

body.text: darśanapatham upayāto 'py apasarasi kuto mameśa bhṛtyasya &

children.text: kṣaṇamātrakam iha na bhavasi kasya na jantor dṛśor viṣayaḥ // UtSst_12.16 //
children.translated_text: You who are not the object of sight for any being even for a moment here — //UtSst 12.16//

body.translated_text: Even though You have come into the range of vision, O Lord, why do You withdraw from me, Your servant?

children.text: plāvanāt paramabhedamānayaṃs tvāṃ nijaṃ ca vapur āpnuyāṃ mudam // UtSst_12.17 //
children.translated_text: bringing about supreme non-difference between You and my own body, shall I attain bliss? //UtSst 12.17//

body.translated_text: When, O all-pervading Lord, by flooding [me] with the continuous stream of the clear nectar of the awareness of unity,

body.text: aham ity amuto 'varuddhalokād bhavadīyāt pratipattisārato me &

children.text: aṇumātrakam eva viśvaniṣṭhaṃ ghaṭatāṃ yena bhaveyam arcitā te // UtSst_12.18 //
children.translated_text: may even the slightest particle, which is the foundation of the universe, be joined [to me], whereby I may be fit for Your worship. //UtSst 12.18//

body.translated_text: From Your [realm] which is beyond the world confined by [the notion of] 'I,' by the essence of my realization,

body.text: aparimitarūpam ahaṃ taṃ taṃ bhāvaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ paśyan &

children.text: tvām eva viśvarūpaṃ nijanāthaṃ sādhu paśyeyam // UtSst_12.19 //
children.translated_text: may I truly see You alone — the Lord of the universe in all forms — as my own master. //UtSst 12.19//

body.translated_text: Seeing moment by moment this and that state in its unlimited form,

body.text: bhavadaṅgagataṃ tam eva kasmān na manaḥ paryaṭatīṣṭam artham artham &

children.text: prakṛtikṣatir asti no tathāsya mama cecchā paripūryate paraiva // UtSst_12.20 //
children.translated_text: There is no impairment of [its] essential nature; rather, the supreme desire of mine is fulfilled [thereby]. //UtSst 12.20//

body.translated_text: Why does the mind, which belongs to Your body, not roam freely through each desired object?

body.text: śataśaḥ kila te tavānubhāvād bhagavan ke 'py amunaiva cakṣuṣā ye &

children.text: api hālikaceṣṭayā carantaḥ paripaśyanti bhavadvapuḥ sadāgre // UtSst_12.21 //
children.translated_text: even while performing the actions of a plowman, constantly behold Your form always before them. //UtSst 12.21//

body.translated_text: By Your power, O Blessed One, there are hundreds of those who, with this very eye,

body.text: na sā matir udeti yā na bhavati tvadicchāmayī sadā śubham athetarad bhagavataivam ācaryate &

children.text: ato 'smi bhavadātmako bhuvi yathā tathā sañcaran sthi to 'niśam abādhitatvadamalaṅghripūjotsavaḥ // UtSst_12.22 //
children.translated_text: therefore, being of Your nature, moving about in the world in whatever way, I remain constantly in the unobstructed festival of worship at Your pure feet. //UtSst 12.22//

body.translated_text: No thought arises that is not always pervaded by Your will — what is auspicious, or otherwise, is accomplished by the Blessed One alone;

body.text: bhavadīyagabhīrabhāṣiteṣu pratibhā samyag udetu me puro 'taḥ &

children.text: tadanuṣṭhitaśaktir apy atas tadbhavadarcāvyasanaṃ ca nirvirāmam // UtSst_12.23 //
children.translated_text: and from that, the power to practice them, and also the unceasing passion for worshiping You. //UtSst 12.23//

body.translated_text: May clear insight arise before me, inwardly, in Your profound teachings;

body.text: vyavahārapade 'pi sarvadā pratibhātv arthakalāpa eṣa mām &

children.text: bhavato 'vayavo yathā na tu svata evādaraṇīyatāṃ gataḥ // UtSst_12.24 //
children.translated_text: as parts of You, and not as having attained venerability on their own. //UtSst 12.24//

body.translated_text: Even in the domain of worldly activity, may this entire aggregate of objects always appear to me

body.text: manasi svarasena yatra tatra pracaraty apy aham asya gocareṣu &

children.text: prasṛto 'py avilola eva yuṣmatparicaryācaturaḥ sadā bhaveyam // UtSst_12.25 //
children.translated_text: though extended [outward], may I be ever unagitated, always skilled in Your service. //UtSst 12.25//

body.translated_text: Even as my mind spontaneously wanders here and there in the domain of its objects,

body.text: bhagavan bhavadicchayaiva dāsas tava jāto 'smi parasya nātra śaktiḥ &

children.text: katham eṣa tathāpi vaktrabimbaṃ tava paśyāmi na jātu citram etat // UtSst_12.26 //
children.translated_text: yet how is it that I never see the reflection of Your face? This is indeed wondrous. //UtSst 12.26//

body.translated_text: O Blessed One, by Your will alone have I become Your servant; no one else has the power [to make me so];

body.text: samutsukās tvāṃ prati ye bhavantaṃ pratyartharūpād avalokayanti &

children.text: teṣām aho kiṃ tadupasthitaṃ syāt kiṃ sādhanaṃ vā phalitaṃ bhavet tat // UtSst_12.27 //
children.translated_text: ah, what has come to them? Or what means has borne fruit for them? //UtSst 12.27//

body.translated_text: Those who, eager toward You, behold You from the standpoint of the reality of each object —

body.text: bhāvā bhāvatayā santu bhavadbhāvena me bhava &

children.text: tathā na kiñcid apy astu na kiñcid bhavato 'nyathā // UtSst_12.28 //
children.translated_text: thus let there be nothing whatsoever — nothing other than You. //UtSst 12.28//

body.translated_text: Let all states exist as states; be my existence through Your existence;

body.text: yan na kiñcid api tanna kiñcid apy astu kiñcid api kiñcid eva me &

children.text: sarvathā bhavatu tāvatā bhavān sarvato bhavati labdhapūjitaḥ // UtSst_12.29 //
children.translated_text: in every way, so far as You are concerned, You are present everywhere, having been worshiped. //UtSst 12.29//

body.translated_text: Whatever is nothing — let that be nothing; whatever is something — let that be something for me;
The Thirteenth Hymn, named the <s>Saṃgrahastotra</s> (Summary Hymn).

body.text: saṃgrahena sukhaduḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ māṃ prati sthitam idaṃ śṛṇu prabho &

children.text: saukhyam eṣa bhavatā samāgamaḥ svāminā viraha eva duḥkhitā // UtSst_13.1 //
children.translated_text: happiness is union with You, the Master; separation alone is suffering. //UtSst 13.1//

body.translated_text: Listen, O Lord, to this that stands as the summary regarding pleasure and pain for me:

body.text: antar apy atitarām aṇīyasī yā tvadaprathanakālikāsti me &

children.text: tām apīśa parimṛjya sarvataḥ svaṃ svarūpam amalaṃ prakāśaya // UtSst_13.2 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, wiping that away completely from all sides, reveal Your own pure nature. //UtSst 13.2//

body.translated_text: Even the most extremely subtle dark veil within me that is the non-manifestation of You —

children.text: tiṣṭhataḥ satatam arcataḥ prabhuṃ jīvitaṃ mṛtam athānyad astu me // UtSst_13.3 //
children.translated_text: whether I live or die, or whatever else may be, let me always stand and worship the Lord. //UtSst 13.3//

body.translated_text: In Your body which pervades the entire universe, which is of the nature of the nectar-essence of consciousness, and which is without end —

body.text: īśvaro 'ham aham eva rūpavān paṇḍito 'smi subhago 'smi ko 'paraḥ &

children.text: matsamo 'sti jagatīti śobhate mānitā tvadanurāgiṇaḥ param // UtSst_13.4 //
children.translated_text: is equal to me in the world?' — this self-esteem shines only in one who is devoted to You. //UtSst 13.4//

body.translated_text: 'I am the Lord, I alone am beautiful, I am learned, I am fortunate — who else

children.text: tad yathāsthitapadārthasaṃvidā māṃ kuruṣva caraṇārcanocitam // UtSst_13.5 //
children.translated_text: make me fit for the worship of [Your] feet. //UtSst 13.5//

body.translated_text: O God of gods, by the awareness of things as they truly are, born from the withdrawal of the proclamation of the nectar of Your non-duality,

body.text: dhyāyate tad anu dṛśyate tataḥ spṛśyate ca parameśvaraḥ svayam &

children.text: yatra pūjanamahotsavaḥ sa me sarvadāstu bhavato 'nubhāvataḥ // UtSst_13.6 //
children.translated_text: may that great festival of worship be mine always, through Your power. //UtSst 13.6//

body.translated_text: First one meditates, then one sees, then one touches the Supreme Lord Himself —

children.text: yugmam etad itaretarāśrayaṃ bhaktiśāliṣu sadā vijṛmbhate // UtSst_13.7 //
children.translated_text: are a pair that mutually depend on each other, [then this pair] always manifests in those who possess devotion. //UtSst 13.7//

body.translated_text: If the vision of things as they truly are and the great festival of worshiping You

children.text: sarvabhāvacaṣakeṣu pūriteṣv āpibann api bhaveyam unmadaḥ // UtSst_13.8 //
children.translated_text: with the cups of all experiences filled, may I even become intoxicated! //UtSst 13.8//

body.translated_text: Continuously, through the gateway of each sense, drinking the elixir of the nectar of worshiping You,

body.text: anyavedyam aṇumātram asti na svaprakāśam akhilaṃ vijṛmbhate &

children.text: yatra nātha bhavataḥ pure sthitaṃ tatra me kuru sadā tavārcituḥ // UtSst_13.9 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, where [I am] established in Your city, there grant me always [the state] of one who worships You. //UtSst 13.9//

body.translated_text: There is not even the slightest thing known by another; everything self-luminous unfolds —

body.text: dāsadhāmni viniyojito 'py ahaṃ svecchayaiva parameśvara tvayā &

children.text: darśanena na kim asmi pātritaḥ pādasaṃvahanakarmaṇāpi vā // UtSst_13.10 //
children.translated_text: am I not also worthy of [Your] vision, or even of the service of massaging [Your] feet? //UtSst 13.10//

body.translated_text: Though I have been assigned to the station of a servant, by Your own free will, O Supreme Lord,

body.text: śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptam īśa na karoṣi karhicit &

children.text: adya māṃ prati kim āgataṃ yataḥ svaprakāśanavidhau vilambase // UtSst_13.11 //
children.translated_text: what has come to pass regarding me today, that You delay in Your self-revelation? //UtSst 13.11//

body.translated_text: At the time of the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>), O Lord, You never make an investigation;

body.text: tatra tatra viṣaye bahirvibhāty antare ca parameśvarīyutam &

children.text: tvāṃ jagattritayanirbharaṃ sadā lokayeya nijapāṇipūjitam // UtSst_13.12 //
children.translated_text: may I always behold You, who pervade all three worlds, worshiped by my own hands. //UtSst 13.12//

body.translated_text: In each and every object shining externally, and internally united with the Supreme Goddess,

children.text: syāṃ prasāda paramāmṛtāsavāpānakeliparilabdhanirvṛtiḥ // UtSst_13.13 //
children.translated_text: may I be one who has attained bliss through the sport of drinking the supreme nectar-elixir of grace. //UtSst 13.13//

body.translated_text: Ascending the palace of the Master at all times, merely by intention, without any obstruction,

children.text: tāṃ samarpayati tena te vapuḥ pūjayanty acalabhaktiśālinaḥ // UtSst_13.14 //
children.translated_text: bestows wonder — by that very [power], those who possess unwavering devotion worship Your form. //UtSst 13.14//

body.translated_text: That which, merely by the act of touching all beautiful and worthy objects,

body.text: sphārayasy akhilam ātmanā sphuran viśvam āmṛśasi rūpam āmṛśan &

children.text: yat svayaṃ nijarasena ghurṇase tat samullasati bhāvamaṇḍalam // UtSst_13.15 //
children.translated_text: that by which You Yourself swirl with Your own essence — that circle of existence shines forth. //UtSst 13.15//

body.translated_text: You expand the entire universe by Yourself, radiating; You apprehend form as You apprehend [it];

body.text: yo 'vikalpam idam arthamaṇḍalaṃ paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ &

children.text: svātmapakṣaparipūrite jagaty asya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam // UtSst_13.16 //
children.translated_text: in a world filled with his own party, what fear has this eternally happy one? //UtSst 13.16//

body.translated_text: He who sees without conceptual construction this entire sphere of objects, O Lord, as Your body —

body.text: kaṇṭhakoṇaviniviṣṭam īśa te kālakūṭam api me mahāmṛtam &

children.text: apy upāttam amṛtaṃ bhavadvapur bhedavṛtti yadi rocate na me // UtSst_13.17 //
children.translated_text: even the nectar taken up [by others] — if it acts as a differentiator from Your body — does not please me. //UtSst 13.17//

body.translated_text: O Lord, the <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) lodged in the corner of Your throat is also great nectar for me;

children.text: syām athāpi bhavadarcanakriyāpreyasīparigatāśayaḥ sadā // UtSst_13.18 //
children.translated_text: and may my mind always be pervaded by the beloved activity of worshiping You. //UtSst 13.18//

body.translated_text: May I be adorned with a face singing love-songs made of delirious talk about You;

body.text: īhitaṃ na bata pārameśvaraṃ śakyate gaṇayituṃ tathā ca me &

children.text: dattam apy amṛtanirbharaṃ vapuḥ svaṃ na pātum anumanyate tathā // UtSst_13.19 //
children.translated_text: even though a body overflowing with nectar has been given, one is not permitted to drink it fully. //UtSst 13.19//

body.translated_text: Alas, the divine will cannot be fathomed; and thus for me,

body.text: tvām agādham avikalpam advayaṃ svaṃ svarūpam akhilārthaghasmaram &

children.text: āviśann aham umeśa sarvadā pūjayeyam abhisaṃstuvīya ca // UtSst_13.20 //
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Umā</s>, may I always worship and praise [You]. //UtSst 13.20//

body.translated_text: Entering You — fathomless, beyond conceptual thought, non-dual, my own true nature, the devourer of all objects —
The Fourteenth Hymn, named the <s>Jayastotra</s> (Victory Hymn).

children.text: jayodghoṣaṇapīyūṣarasam āsvādaye kṣaṇam // UtSst_14.1 //
children.translated_text: let me savor for a moment the nectar-essence of the proclamation of victory. //UtSst 14.1//

body.translated_text: Before my own Master, who is the treasury of the splendor of victory,

children.text: pārvatīpraṇayiñ śarva sarvagīrvāṇapūrvaja // UtSst_14.2 //
children.translated_text: the beloved of <s>Pārvatī</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, the firstborn of all the gods! //UtSst 14.2//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one <s>Rudra</s>, the one <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: jaya pītartalokārtikālakūṭāṅkakandhara // UtSst_14.3 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose neck bears the mark of the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison drunk to remove the world's affliction! //UtSst 14.3//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one whose mark is being the sole lord of the three worlds, O three-eyed one!

children.text: jayecchāmātrasiddārthapūjārhacaraṇāmbuja // UtSst_14.4 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose lotus-feet are worthy of worship, and whose purposes are accomplished by mere will! //UtSst 14.4//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one whose hand gleams with the trident embodying the three powers in manifest form!

children.text: jayaikajaṭikākṣīṇagaṅgākṛtyāttabhasmaka // UtSst_14.5 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one adorned with ashes, who bears the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in a single matted lock, undiminished! //UtSst 14.5//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who bears a transcendent body streaming with hundreds of beauties!

children.text: jayeśvarāṅgasaṅgottharatnakāntāhimaṇḍana // UtSst_14.6 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one adorned with serpent-jewels arisen from contact with the Goddess's body! //UtSst 14.6//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one anointed with the moonlight-shadow spread over the milk-ocean!

children.text: jaya gaṅgāsadārbdhaviśvaiśvaryābhiṣecana // UtSst_14.7 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one consecrated with universal sovereignty by the eternally surging <s>Gaṅgā</s>! //UtSst 14.7//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one whose refuge resembles the imperishable single crescent moon!

children.text: jaya bhaktimadābaddhagoṣṭhīniyatasannidhe // UtSst_14.8 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose presence is ever fixed in the assembly of those bound by the intoxication of devotion! //UtSst 14.8//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who purified the herd of cows by the touch of [His] lower body!

children.text: jaya gaurīpariṣvaṅgayogyasaubhāgyabhājana // UtSst_14.9 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one who is a vessel of good fortune worthy of <s>Gaurī</s>'s embrace! //UtSst 14.9//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who playfully deceives the naive by the pretense of voluntary austerity!

children.text: jaya bhaktimadoddāmabhaktavāṅnṛttatoṣita // UtSst_14.10 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one who is pleased by the speech and dance of devotees intoxicated with the rapture of devotion! //UtSst 14.10//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who is eager for offerings of moods softened by the moisture of the nectar of devotion!

children.text: jayalokeśvaraśreṇiśirovidhṛtaśāsana // UtSst_14.11 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose command is upheld on the heads of the hosts of world-lords! //UtSst 14.11//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one whose power is the source and dissolution of the majesty of gods from <s>Brahmā</s> onward!

children.text: jayātmadānaparyantaviśveśvaramaheśvara // UtSst_14.12 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the Great Lord of the universe, whose [giving extends] even to the gift of Self! //UtSst 14.12//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one whose glory is manifest through his own seal impressed upon the entire universe!

children.text: jayaiśvaryabharodvāhadevīmātrasahāyaka // UtSst_14.13 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose sole companion in bearing the burden of sovereignty is the Goddess alone! //UtSst 14.13//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who is without a second even at the opportune moment of creating the three worlds!

children.text: jayāvigītam ābālagīyamāneśvaradhvane // UtSst_14.14 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose divine sound is sung unceasingly even from childhood! //UtSst 14.14//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who has pervaded all three worlds simultaneously!

children.text: jaya bhīṣmamahāmṛtyughaṭanāpūrvabhairava // UtSst_14.15 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the awesome <s>Bhairava</s>, unprecedented in the workings of dreadful great death! //UtSst 14.15//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who is innately exalted, without depending on qualities such as compassion!

children.text: jaya śreyaḥśataguṇānuganāmānukīrtana // UtSst_14.16 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose names, following [qualities] hundredfold greater than [mere] blessedness, are celebrated! //UtSst 14.16//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who has no adversary in the fierce activity of universal dissolution!

children.text: jaya viśvakṣayakṣepikṣaṇakopāśuśukṣaṇe // UtSst_14.17 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one who by a moment's anger dries up [the world] and casts away universal dissolution! //UtSst 14.17//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who has playfully traversed this ocean, the mine of nectar!

children.text: jaya prasuptajagatījāgarūkādhipūruṣa // UtSst_14.18 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the supreme Person who is ever-wakeful over the sleeping world! //UtSst 14.18//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who is the sole lamp for living beings blinded by the darkness of delusion!

children.text: jaya sanmānasavyomavilāsivarasārasa // UtSst_14.19 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the excellent royal swan sporting in the sky of pure mind! //UtSst 14.19//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who is the life-giving bird singing in the groves of the mountain of the body!

children.text: jaya pāpiṣu nindolkāpātanotpātacandramaḥ // UtSst_14.20 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the moon that causes the falling of the firebrand of reproach upon sinners! //UtSst 14.20//

body.translated_text: Victory to the Lord of the mountain from whose heights arise lofty golden minerals!

children.text: jaya sarvadaśārūḍhabhaktimallokalokita // UtSst_14.21 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one who is beheld by the devotee-wrestlers mounted in every state, intoxicated with devotion! //UtSst 14.21//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who is difficult to approach even by sages and gods afflicted by harsh austerities!

children.text: jaya prapannajanatālālanaikaprayojana // UtSst_14.22 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose sole purpose is the nurturing of those who have surrendered! //UtSst 14.22//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one who has made his own dependents into messengers of the expansion of his own prosperity!

children.text: jaya bhaktimadālolalīlotpalamagotsava // UtSst_14.23 //
children.translated_text: Victory to the one whose festive play is the playful blue lotus swaying in the intoxication of devotion! //UtSst 14.23//

body.translated_text: Victory to the one whose sole glorious deed is being the cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction!

body.text: jaya jayabhājana jaya jitajanmajarāmaraṇa jaya jagajjyeṣṭha &

children.text: jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya tryakṣa // UtSst_14.24 //
children.translated_text: Victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, O three-eyed one! //UtSst 14.24//

body.translated_text: Victory, O vessel of victory! Victory, O conqueror of birth, old age, and death! Victory, O eldest of the universe!
The Fifteenth Hymn, named the <s>Bhaktistotra</s> (Devotion Hymn).

children.text: yoginaḥ paṇḍitāḥ svasthās tvadbhaktā eva tattvataḥ // UtSst_15.1 //
children.translated_text: [but only] Your devotees are truly <s>yogīs</s>, scholars, and self-possessed. //UtSst 15.1//

body.translated_text: There are texts that cleanse the three impurities, and those who have crossed beyond them;

children.text: caranti sukhino nātha bhaktimanto jagattaṭe // UtSst_15.2 //
children.translated_text: the devotees move about happily, O Lord, on the shore of the world. //UtSst 15.2//

body.translated_text: Nourished by the sustenance of desire and the like, subject to the constraint of time belonging to <s>māyā</s>,

body.text: rudanto vā hasanto vā tvām uccaiḥ pralapanty amī &

children.text: bhaktāḥ stutipadoccāropacārāḥ pṛthag eva te // UtSst_15.3 //
children.translated_text: Your devotees are of a different order altogether, [even though they seem to perform] the gestures of uttering words of praise. //UtSst 15.3//

body.translated_text: Whether weeping or laughing, they proclaim You aloud;

body.text: na virakto na cāpīśo mokṣākāṅkṣī tvadarcakaḥ &

children.text: bhaveyam api tūdriktabhaktyāsavarasonmadaḥ // UtSst_15.4 //
children.translated_text: may I also become intoxicated with the overflowing flavor of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) and <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment).

body.translated_text: Your worshiper is neither detached nor, O Lord, desirous of liberation;

children.text: tvām īśa bhaktipīyūṣarasapūrair namāmi tam // UtSst_15.5 //
children.translated_text: I bow to him, filled with the nectarean essence of <s>bhakti</s>.

body.translated_text: He who worships You, O Lord, by drawing the external into the very interior of the heart —

children.text: sukhaduḥkhātmanor bhaktāḥ kim apy āsvādayanty aho // UtSst_15.6 //
children.translated_text: as well as pleasure and pain — devotees savor something indescribable, alas!

body.translated_text: Within the pairs of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, action and knowledge,

body.text: carācarapitaḥ svāmin apy andhā api kuṣṭhinaḥ &

children.text: śobhante param uddāmabhavadbhaktivibhūṣaṇāḥ // UtSst_15.7 //
children.translated_text: shine supremely, adorned with unbounded devotion to You.

body.translated_text: O Father of all moving and unmoving beings, O Master, even the blind and the leprous

children.text: bhavadbhaktimahoṣmaṇo rājarājam apīśate // UtSst_15.8 //
children.translated_text: through the great warmth of devotion to You, rule even over the king of kings.

body.translated_text: Even those whose limbs are shaded by beds of gathered grass and peacock feathers, O Lord,

children.text: cetasaiva vibho 'rcanti kecit tvām abhitaḥ sthitāḥ // UtSst_15.9 //
children.translated_text: some worship You with mind alone, O All-pervading Lord, stationed all around.

body.translated_text: Rolling in the nectar-moist devotion to You, though wishing to rise,

children.text: saṃsāradurgatiharaṃ bhavadbhaktimahādhanam // UtSst_15.10 //
children.translated_text: is to be protected, increased, and greatly honored.

body.translated_text: This great treasure of devotion to You, O Lord, which removes the evil destinies of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text: nātha te bhaktajanatā yady api tvayi rāgiṇī &

children.text: tathāpīrṣyāṃ vihāyāsyās tuṣṭāstu svāminī sadā // UtSst_15.11 //
children.translated_text: may Your consort, setting aside jealousy, be ever pleased with them.

body.translated_text: O Lord, though the community of Your devotees is passionately attached to You,

children.text: labdhe dugdhamahākumbhe hatā dadhani gṛdhnutā // UtSst_15.12 //
children.translated_text: like one who craves buttermilk when a great pot of milk has been obtained — (other desires) are destroyed.

body.translated_text: Your very state of being is the future that awaits; when devotion to You has arisen —

body.text: kim iyaṃ na siddhir atulā kiṃ vā mukhyaṃ na saukhyam āsravati &

children.text: bhaktir upacīyamānā yeyaṃ śambhoḥ sadātanī bhavati // UtSst_15.13 //
children.translated_text: This devotion to <s>Śambhu</s>, which, when cultivated, becomes eternal.

body.translated_text: Is this not an incomparable <s>siddhi</s> (attainment)? Does it not yield supreme happiness? —

children.text: na nijān api tanute tānapauruṣeyān svasampadullāsān // UtSst_15.14 //
children.translated_text: does not display even its own superhuman splendors and magnificences.

body.translated_text: Alas, the jewel-vine of devotion to You, submerged in my impure mind,

body.text: bhaktir bhagavati bhavati trilokanāthe nanūttamā siddhiḥ &

children.text: kiṃ tv aṇimādikavirahāt saiva na pūrṇeti cintā me // UtSst_15.15 //
children.translated_text: but my concern is that without <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and other powers, it may not be complete.

body.translated_text: Devotion to the <s>Bhagavat</s>, the Lord of the three worlds, is indeed the supreme <s>siddhi</s>;

children.text: vāsayanty api viruddhavāsanān yogino nikaṭavāsino 'khilān // UtSst_15.16 //
children.translated_text: perfume even all yogins dwelling nearby, even those of contrary dispositions.

body.translated_text: The auspicious fragrances of hymns to <s>Tryambaka</s> (Three-Eyed <s>Śiva</s>), flashing forth intensely both outwardly and inwardly,

body.text: jyotir asti kathayāpi na kiṃ cid viśvam apy atisuṣuptam aśeṣam &

children.text: yatra nātha śivarātripade 'smin nityam arcayati bhaktajanas tvām // UtSst_15.17 //
children.translated_text: yet in this moment of <s>Śivarātri</s>, O Lord, the community of devotees perpetually worships You.

body.translated_text: There is no light whatsoever, nor any tale to tell; the entire universe is in profound sleep —

body.text: sattvaṃ satyaguṇe śive bhagavati sphārībhavatv arcane cūḍāyāṃ vilasantu śaṅkarapadaprodyadrajaḥsaṅcayāḥ &

children.text: rāgādismṛtivāsanām api samucchettuṃ tamo jṛmbhatāṃ śambho me bhavatāt tvadātmavilaye traiguṇyavargo 'thavā // UtSst_15.18 //
children.translated_text: may <s>tamas</s> expand to cut off even the latent impressions of attachment and the rest — or rather, O <s>Śambhu</s>, may the entire group of the three <s>guṇas</s> dissolve into You.

body.translated_text: May <s>sattva</s> expand in the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s> of true qualities; may the clusters of dust arising from <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s feet shine upon the crown;

body.text: saṃsārādhvā sudūraḥ kharataravividhavyādhidagdhāṅgayaṣṭiḥ bhogā naivopabhuktā yad api sukham abhūj jātu nanno cirāya &

children.text: itthaṃ vyartho 'smi jātaḥ śaśidharacaraṇākrāntikāntottamāṅgas tvadbhaktaś ceti tan me kuru sapadi mahāsampado dīrghadīrghāḥ // UtSst_15.19 //
children.translated_text: thus I have become worthless; yet my glorious head is graced by the touch of the Moon-Bearer's feet, and I am Your devotee — therefore grant me at once great and enduring treasures.

body.translated_text: The road of <s>saṃsāra</s> is immensely long, the body is scorched by ever more severe and various diseases; pleasures have not been truly enjoyed, and whatever happiness there was never lasted long —
The sixteenth hymn, named <s>Pāśānudbhedana</s> (Breaking of Bonds).

body.text: na kiñcid eva lokānāṃ bhavadāvaraṇaṃ prati \var{yat kiṃ cid eva bhūtānāṃ\em \cit \Naresvaraparīksā} &

children.text: na kiñcid eva bhaktānāṃ bhavadāvaraṇaṃ prati // UtSst_16.1 //
children.translated_text: there is nothing at all among devotees that serves as a veil against You.

body.translated_text: There is nothing at all among worldly beings that serves as a veil against You;

children.text: bhaktibhājāṃ bhavān ātmā sakṛc chuddho 'vabhāsate // UtSst_16.2 //
children.translated_text: You, the Self, shine forth at once, pure, to those who possess <s>bhakti</s>.

body.translated_text: Though attainable only through a sequence of means, though crowded with qualifications,

body.text: jayanto 'pi hasanty ete jitā api hasanti ca &

children.text: bhavadbhaktisudhāpānamattāḥ ke 'py eva ye prabho // UtSst_16.3 //
children.translated_text: those certain ones, O Lord, who are intoxicated by drinking the nectar of devotion to You.

body.translated_text: Whether conquering, they laugh, and even when conquered, they laugh —

body.text: śuṣkakaṃ maiva siddheya maiva mucyeya vāpi tu &

children.text: svādiṣṭhaparakāṣṭāptatvadbhaktirasanirbharaḥ // UtSst_16.4 //
children.translated_text: being filled with the essence of devotion to You, which has reached the pinnacle of deliciousness.

body.translated_text: May I never attain dry <s>siddhi</s>, nor even liberation —

children.text: ghaṭitas tadvad īśāna sa eva paripuṣyatu // UtSst_16.5 //
children.translated_text: so, O <s>Īśāna</s>, may that very same flavor be nourished.

body.translated_text: Just as this flavor of devotion to You arose in me though previously unknown,

children.text: kevalaṃ sa tathā ko 'pi bhaktyāveśo 'stu me sadā // UtSst_16.6 //
children.translated_text: only let there be in me always that certain indescribable possession by <s>bhakti</s>.

body.translated_text: Truly, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, I have no other scope of prayer;

children.text: tathā haseyaṃ udyāṃ ca raṭeyaṃ ca śivety alam // UtSst_16.7 //
children.translated_text: may I laugh, may I leap up, and may I cry out '<s>Śiva</s>!' unceasingly.

body.translated_text: Though intoxicated with devotion, may I rage, may I lie prostrate in existence,

body.text: viṣamastho 'pi svastho 'pi rudann api hasann api &

children.text: gambhīro 'pi vicitto 'pi bhaveyaṃ bhaktitaḥ prabho // UtSst_16.8 //
children.translated_text: whether grave or distracted — may I be so through devotion, O Lord.

body.translated_text: Whether in adversity or in ease, whether weeping or laughing,

body.text: bhaktānāṃ nāsti saṃvedyaṃ tvadantar yadi vā bahiḥ &

children.text: ciddharmā yatra na bhavān nirvikalpaḥ sthitaḥ svayam // UtSst_16.9 //
children.translated_text: where You, whose nature is consciousness, do not abide, free of conceptual thought.

body.translated_text: For devotees there is no object of experience, whether within You or outside,

children.text: hṛṣyanty evāntarāviddhās tīkṣṇaromāñcasūcibhiḥ // UtSst_16.10 //
children.translated_text: rejoice as if touched by drops of Your nectar, pierced within by the sharp needles of horripilation.

body.translated_text: Devotees, even when reproach of You is imitated,

children.text: yeṣāṃ sudhārdrā sarvaiva saṃvit tvaccandrikāmayī // UtSst_16.11 //
children.translated_text: for whom all awareness, moist with nectar, is made of Your moonlight.

body.translated_text: Even painful sensation serves as enjoyment for those possessing devotion,

children.text: nirvyājaṃ tvadvapuḥsparśarasāsvādasukhaṃ samam // UtSst_16.12 //
children.translated_text: the bliss of savoring the touch of Your body is equal and unfeigned.

body.translated_text: For devotees confined here or there, within or without,

children.text: vilupyāsvādayanty eke vapur acchaṃ sudhāmayam // UtSst_16.13 //
children.translated_text: savor the pure body made of nectar.

body.translated_text: Some, O Lord, in the worship of devotion to You, removing the element of wretchedness that depends on duality,

body.text: bhrāntās tīrthadṛśo bhinnā bhrānter eva hi bhinnatā &

children.text: niṣpratidvandvi vastv ekaṃ bhaktānāṃ tvaṃ tu rājase // UtSst_16.14 //
children.translated_text: but You shine as the one Reality without opposition for devotees.

body.translated_text: The deluded see holy places as different; diversity arises from delusion alone;

children.text: yasyāsau bhaktimāṃl lokatulyaśīlaḥ kathaṃ bhavet // UtSst_16.15 //
children.translated_text: how could such a devotee be of a disposition equal to worldly people?

body.translated_text: One whose mind is purified by the ripening away of honor, dishonor, attachment, and the rest —

children.text: teṣāṃ mahīyasām agre katame jñānaśālinaḥ // UtSst_16.16 //
children.translated_text: before those great ones, who are the possessors of knowledge?

body.translated_text: Those in whom the darkness of attachment and aversion has been conquered by the radiance of devotion —

children.text: tasya prārabdhamadhyāntadaśāsūccaiḥ sukhāsikā // UtSst_16.17 //
children.translated_text: the seat of supreme bliss is elevated in the beginning, middle, and end states.

body.translated_text: For one whose practice consists of bathing in and drinking the nectar of devotion,

body.text: kīrtyaś cintāpadaṃ mṛgyaḥ pūjyo yena tvam eva tat &

children.text: bhavadbhaktimatāṃ ślāghyā lokayātrā bhavanmayī // UtSst_16.18 //
children.translated_text: the praiseworthy worldly life of those possessing devotion to You, which is entirely pervaded by You.

body.translated_text: By whatever means You are to be celebrated, contemplated, sought, and worshipped — that constitutes

body.text: muktisaṃjñā vipakvāyā bhakter eva tvayi prabho &

children.text: tasyām ādyadaśārūḍhā muktakalpā vayaṃ tataḥ // UtSst_16.19 //
children.translated_text: having ascended to the initial stage of that, we are therefore virtually liberated.

body.translated_text: 'Liberation' is simply the name for devotion to You, O Lord, that has fully ripened;

children.text: tvatparācī vibho mā bhūd api saukhyaparamparā // UtSst_16.20 //
children.translated_text: but may there never be, O All-pervading Lord, even a succession of pleasures turned away from You.

body.translated_text: May even an abundance of suffering come to me, whose self is filled with devotion to You;

body.text: tvaṃ bhaktyā prīyase bhaktiḥ prīte tvayi ca nātha yat &

children.text: tadanyonyāśrayaṃ yuktaṃ yathā vettha tvam eva tat // UtSst_16.21 //
children.translated_text: that mutual dependence is fitting; how it works, You alone know.

body.translated_text: You are pleased by devotion, and devotion arises because You are pleased, O Lord —

body.text: sākāro vā nirākaro vāntar vā bahir eva vā &

children.text: bhaktimattātmanāṃ nātha sarvathāsi sudhāmayaḥ // UtSst_16.22 //
children.translated_text: for those whose selves are possessed of devotion, O Lord, You are in every way made of nectar.

body.translated_text: Whether with form or formless, whether within or without —

body.text: asminn eva jagaty antar bhavadbhaktimataḥ prati &

children.text: harṣaprakāśanaphalam anyad eva jagatsthitam // UtSst_16.23 //
children.translated_text: the rest of the world exists only for the purpose of manifesting joy.

body.translated_text: Within this very world, for one possessing devotion to You,

body.text: guhye bhaktiḥ pare bhaktir bhaktir viśvamaheśvare &

children.text: tvayi śambhau śive deva bhaktir nāma kim apy aho // UtSst_16.24 //
children.translated_text: devotion to You, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, O God — what an indescribable thing is this called devotion!

body.translated_text: Devotion to the Secret One, devotion to the Supreme, devotion to the Great Lord of the Universe —

body.text: bhaktir bhaktiḥ pare bhaktir bhaktir nāma samutkaṭā &

children.text: tāraṃ viraumi yat tīvrā bhaktir me 'stu paraṃ tvayi // UtSst_16.25 //
children.translated_text: I cry aloud: may fierce devotion to You be mine supremely.

body.translated_text: Devotion! Devotion! Devotion to the Supreme! Devotion — that name, intensely exalted!

children.text: tvayi lagnam anarghaṃ syād ratnam vā yadi vā tṛṇam // UtSst_16.26 //
children.translated_text: whatever is attached to You would be priceless — whether a jewel or a blade of grass.

body.translated_text: Since I am the ground from which all beauties are born, O Lord,

body.text: āvedakād ā ca vedyād yeṣāṃ saṃvedanādhvani &

children.text: bhavatā na viyogo 'sti te jayanti bhavajjuṣaḥ // UtSst_16.27 //
children.translated_text: there is no separation from You, they triumph, those who are devoted to You.

body.translated_text: Those for whom, on the path of experience — from the cognizer to the cognized —

children.text: svāmin parais tu tatraiva tāmyadbhis tyaktayantraṇaiḥ // UtSst_16.28 //
children.translated_text: but by others, O Master, right there within it, exhausted and having abandoned all restraint.

body.translated_text: By some, outside the assembly-hall of <s>saṃsāra</s>, You are embraced;

children.text: pralayotsavasarabhasayā dṛḍham upagūḍhaṃ śivaṃ vande // UtSst_16.29 //
children.translated_text: and who is eager for the festival of dissolution.

body.translated_text: I worship <s>Śiva</s>, firmly embraced by <s>Śivā</s> (the Goddess) — she who has drunk, eaten, adorned herself with, and enjoyed the entire universe,

body.text: parameśvaratā jayaty apūrvā tava viśveśa yadīśitavyaśūnyā &

children.text: aparāpi tathaiva te yayedaṃ jagad ābhāti yathā tathā na bhāti // UtSst_16.30 //
children.translated_text: and equally victorious is that other power of Yours by which this world appears just as it does not appear.

body.translated_text: Victorious is that unprecedented supreme lordship of Yours, O Lord of the Universe, which is devoid of anything to be ruled;
The seventeenth hymn, named <s>Divyakrīḍābahumānana</s> (Honoring Divine Play).

body.text: aho ko 'pi jayaty eṣa svāduḥ pūjāmahotsavaḥ &

children.text: yato 'mṛtarasāsvādam aśrūṇy api dadaty alam // UtSst_17.1 //
children.translated_text: from which even tears abundantly give the taste of nectar!

body.translated_text: Oh, victorious is this indescribable sweet great festival of worship,

children.text: bhaktānāṃ tvanmayāḥ sarve svayaṃ siddhaya eva te // UtSst_17.2 //
children.translated_text: for devotees, pervaded by You, they are all themselves <s>siddhis</s>.

body.translated_text: All endeavors that are preceded by worship of You grant <s>siddhi</s> (attainment);

children.text: tvām arcayanty aviśrantaṃ ye mamaite 'dhidevatāḥ // UtSst_17.3 //
children.translated_text: they are my presiding deities.

body.translated_text: Those who worship You ceaselessly — You who are of all forms, in all states, at all times, simultaneously —

children.text: pūjāvidhir iti khyāto bhaktānāṃ sa sadās tu me // UtSst_17.4 //
children.translated_text: that which is known as the rite of worship for devotees — may that always be mine.

body.translated_text: The festival of touching You, attained by transcending the toil of meditation —

children.text: tvadbhāvarasapīyūṣarasennaiṣāṃ sadārcanam // UtSst_17.5 //
children.translated_text: their perpetual worship is conducted with the nectarean essence of the flavor of awareness of You.

body.translated_text: For devotees it is always the equinox, whose essence is equality;

children.text: pūjātmāsau kriyā tasyāḥ kartāras tvajjuṣaḥ param // UtSst_17.6 //
children.translated_text: of that worship-natured action, those devoted to You alone are the performers.

body.translated_text: That worship which has neither beginning nor end, nor temporal sequence, O Lord —

children.text: yeṣāṃ svapne 'pi mohe 'pi sthitas tvatpūjanotsavaḥ // UtSst_17.7 //
children.translated_text: those in whom the festival of worshipping You persists even in dream and even in delusion.

body.translated_text: They rule even over <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, and they are the partakers of good fortune —

body.text: japatāṃ juhvatāṃ snātāṃ dhyāyatāṃ na ca kevalam &

children.text: bhaktānāṃ bhavadabhyarcāmaho yāvad yadā tadā // UtSst_17.8 //
children.translated_text: but the great worship of devotees extends to You whenever and however far it reaches.

body.translated_text: Not only of those who chant, who offer oblations, who have bathed, who meditate —

children.text: indrādīnām atha brahmamukhyānām asti kaḥ samaḥ // UtSst_17.9 //
children.translated_text: among <s>Indra</s> and the others, or among those headed by <s>Brahmā</s>, who is their equal?

body.translated_text: For those who are always blissful through the enjoyment of tasting the nectar of worship of You —

children.text: yatprāpyaṃ prāpyate kiṃcid bhaktā eva vidanti tat // UtSst_17.10 //
children.translated_text: whatever attainment is attained therein, only devotees know that.

body.translated_text: In the great festival of worship of You, which alone generates the agitation of the universe —

children.text: kāyavākcittaceṣṭādyair arcaye tvāṃ sadā vibho // UtSst_17.11 //
children.translated_text: through the movements of body, speech, and mind, I worship You always, O All-pervading Lord.

body.translated_text: Abiding in Your luminous abode of consciousness, through the activities of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>,

children.text: prayātu kālaḥ sakalo 'py ananto 'pīyadarthaye // UtSst_17.12 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of my bliss of enjoying the uninterrupted worship of You.

body.translated_text: May all time, even if infinite, pass by

children.text: vivardhatām anudinaṃ sadā ca phalatāṃ mama // UtSst_17.13 //
children.translated_text: grow day by day and always bear fruit.

body.translated_text: May my passionate desire for the enjoyment of the nectarean essence of worshipping You, O Lord,

children.text: tvadabdhau tvāṃ mahātmānam arcannāsīya sarvadā // UtSst_17.14 //
children.translated_text: may I abide forever, worshipping You, the Great Self.

body.translated_text: In Your ocean, overflowing with the single essence of nectar born from the dissolution of the world,

children.text: mano nivedyate bhaktaiḥ svādu pūjāvidhau tava // UtSst_17.15 //
children.translated_text: is sweetly offered by devotees in the rite of Your worship.

body.translated_text: The mind, made perpetually straight by the cutting of all knots of latent impressions,

children.text: bhaktānāṃ preṣayanti svatpūjārtham amṛtāsavam // UtSst_17.16 //
children.translated_text: send forth, for devotees, the distillation of nectar for the purpose of Your worship.

body.translated_text: Having presided over the sense-objects, these functions of the faculties

children.text: ko 'nyo nirvāṇahetuḥ syāt tvatpūjāmṛtamajjanāt // UtSst_17.17 //
children.translated_text: what other cause of <s>nirvāṇa</s> could there be than immersion in the nectar of Your worship?

body.translated_text: For devotees whose selves are overpowered by the great heat of the fervor of devotion,

children.text: tvatprasādaikasamprāptihetur me nātha kalpatām // UtSst_17.18 //
children.translated_text: serve perpetually as the sole cause of attaining Your grace, O Lord.

body.translated_text: May the great festival of drinking the nectar of worshipping Your feet

children.text: bhavatpūjāmṛtāpānamadāsvādamahāmudam // UtSst_17.19 //
children.translated_text: the great delight of tasting the intoxication of drinking the nectar of Your worship.

body.translated_text: May I experience ceaselessly, O <s>Īśāna</s>, moment by moment,

children.text: tadaiva yad asambhāvyaṃ sukham āsvādayanti te // UtSst_17.20 //
children.translated_text: for at that very moment they taste an inconceivable bliss.

body.translated_text: The great endeavor of worshipping You is directly meaningful for devotees,

children.text: tāvan nāsvādito manye lavo 'pi sukhasampadaḥ // UtSst_17.21 //
children.translated_text: I consider that not even a fraction of the wealth of happiness has been tasted.

body.translated_text: Until the great festival of tasting the nectar of Your worship has been obtained,

children.text: ayatnasiddhaṃ tvaddhāmasthitiḥ pūjāsu jāyate // UtSst_17.22 //
children.translated_text: the abiding in Your luminous abode arises effortlessly in worship.

body.translated_text: For devotees, without the apparent effort of seeking sense objects,

body.text: na prāpyam asti bhaktanāṃ nāpy eṣām asti durlabham &

children.text: kevalaṃ vicaranty ete bhavatpūjāmadonmadāḥ // UtSst_17.23 //
children.translated_text: they simply wander about, intoxicated with the joy of worshipping You.

body.translated_text: There is nothing for devotees to attain, nor is anything difficult for them to obtain;

children.text: slāghyaḥ pūjāvidhiḥ ko 'pi yo na yācñākalaṃkitaḥ // UtSst_17.24 //
children.translated_text: performed by those whose hearts are generous through the weight of devotion — a worship not blemished by entreaty.

body.translated_text: Ah, how praiseworthy is that indescribable rite of worship to You, O Granter of Boons,

body.text: kā na śobhā na ko hlādaḥ kā samṛddhir na vāparā &

children.text: ko vā na mokṣaḥ ko 'py eṣa mahādevo yad arcyate // UtSst_17.25 //
children.translated_text: and what is not liberation — when this incomprehensible <s>Mahādeva</s> is worshipped?

body.translated_text: What beauty is there that is not found, what delight is not there, what prosperity is not supreme,

children.text: bhavatpūjopayogāya śarīram idam astu me // UtSst_17.26 //
children.translated_text: may this body of mine serve for the worship of You.

body.translated_text: Nourished by the crystal-clear nectar of devotion shining within,

children.text: bhūyāsaṃ jagatām īśa ekaḥ svacchandaceṣṭitaḥ // UtSst_17.27 //
children.translated_text: may I become, O Lord of the worlds, one who acts according to his own will.

body.translated_text: Always dependent upon the enjoyment of worshipping Your feet, O All-pervading Lord,

children.text: jāyate śītalasvādu bhavatpūjāmahāsaraḥ // UtSst_17.28 //
children.translated_text: there arises the cool and sweet great lake of Your worship.

body.translated_text: For some, O Lord, in whom there is thirst for meditation on You, seeing You, and touching You,

children.text: tatheśa bhaktimān eva pūjāsambhogabhājanam // UtSst_17.29 //
children.translated_text: so too, O Lord, only the devotee is the vessel for the enjoyment of worship.

body.translated_text: Just as You alone are the vessel for the enjoyment of the world's worship,

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśato 'pi tattvānāṃ kṣobho yatrollasaty alam // UtSst_17.30 //
children.translated_text: in which the agitation of even the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> fully shines forth.

body.translated_text: Victorious is that indescribable great festival of Your worship, O Master,

children.text: pūjyāny eva bhavanti tvatpūjopakaraṇāny api // UtSst_17.31 //
children.translated_text: even the implements of Your worship become worthy of worship.

body.translated_text: Homage to those, O All-pervading Lord, by the waters of whose devotional nectar

children.text: svātmany eva pare bhaktā mānti harṣeṇa na kvacit // UtSst_17.32 //
children.translated_text: Devotees of the Supreme [who resides] in their own Self rejoice with delight, [finding joy] nowhere else. // UtSst_17.32 //

body.translated_text: At the commencement of worship, O All-pervading Lord, having meditated upon Your essential nature as designated by <s>mantra</s> —

children.text: sudhāsavena sakalā jagatī saṃvibhajyate // UtSst_17.33 //
children.translated_text: the entire world is shared with the nectar-liquor [of devotion]. // UtSst_17.33 //

body.translated_text: By some, blooming [with joy] as if from gaining a kingdom, at the great festival of worship,

children.text: kiṃ devā uta muktās te kiṃ vā ke 'py eva te janāḥ // UtSst_17.34 //
children.translated_text: are they gods, or liberated beings, or are they simply some extraordinary people? // UtSst_17.34 //

body.translated_text: Those whose enjoyment at every moment consists in drinking the nectar of worship —

children.text: aho kim api bhaktānāṃ kim apy eva ca lāghavam // UtSst_17.35 //
children.translated_text: what an ineffable greatness of the devotees, and what an ineffable humility [of the Lord]! // UtSst_17.35 //

body.translated_text: O wonder! By the Lord of all, who has become an instrument of worship —

children.text: bhaktānāṃ kṣīrajaladhikṣobhād iva divaukasām // UtSst_17.36 //
children.translated_text: just as [nectar arose] for the gods from the churning of the milk-ocean. // UtSst_17.36 //

body.translated_text: The surge of nectar arises for devotees from the agitation of the casting of worship-filled offerings,

body.text: pūjāṃ ke cana manyante dhenuṃ kāmadughām iva &

children.text: sudhādhārādhikarasāṃ dhayanty antarmukhāḥ pare // UtSst_17.37 //
children.translated_text: others, turned inward, drink [its milk], richer in flavor than streams of nectar. // UtSst_17.37 //

body.translated_text: Some regard worship as a wish-fulfilling cow;

children.text: upanīya kim apy antaḥ puṣṇāty arcāmahotsavam // UtSst_17.38 //
children.translated_text: having led something within, nourishes the great festival of worship. // UtSst_17.38 //

body.translated_text: Even this casting of offerings by devotees, honored in the world,

children.text: citraṃ dainyāya no yāvad dīnatāyāḥ paraṃ phalam // UtSst_17.39 //
children.translated_text: how wonderful that it does not lead to wretchedness, since the supreme fruit of humility [is thereby attained]! // UtSst_17.39 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, worship of you, who are one's own Self, [arises] by the force of devotion's agitation —

children.text: bhaktānāṃ bhavadaikātmyanirvṛttiprasaras tu saḥ // UtSst_17.40 //
children.translated_text: but for devotees, it is the overflowing bliss of oneness with you. // UtSst_17.40 //

body.translated_text: For some, worship is a stepping-stone of ritual service for attaining your feet;

children.text: vitanyamānā labhate pratiṣṭhāṃ tvayi kām api // UtSst_17.41 //
children.translated_text: [such worship] attains a certain established position in you. // UtSst_17.41 //

body.translated_text: Even when performed with the unbridled abandonment of devotion's intoxication, in forms of worship that seem incoherent,

children.text: śambho tvam eva lalitaḥ pūjānāṃ kila bhājanam // UtSst_17.42 //
children.translated_text: fallen from minds become motionless through the savoring of the sweet <s>rasa</s> (essence) of devotion. // UtSst_17.42 //

body.translated_text: O <s>Śambhu</s>, you alone are the graceful vessel of worships

children.text: bhavatpūjāvidhau nātha sādhanāni bhavantu me // UtSst_17.43 //
children.translated_text: filled with devotion, and steadfast, O Lord. // UtSst_17.43 //

body.translated_text: May my instruments for the rite of worshipping you be complete, pure,

children.text: aho karaṇavṛndasya kāpi lakṣmīr vijṛmbhate // UtSst_17.44 //
children.translated_text: oh, what an ineffable splendor of the assembly of senses blossoms forth! // UtSst_17.44 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, in the act of worshipping you, the treasury of all worthy worship —

body.text: eṣā peśalimā nātha tavaiva kila dṛśyate &

children.text: viśveśvaro 'pi bhṛtyair yad arcyase yaś ca labhyase // UtSst_17.45 //
children.translated_text: that although you are the Lord of the universe, you are worshipped by your servants and are attained [by them]. // UtSst_17.45 //

body.translated_text: This graciousness, O Lord, is seen to be yours alone indeed —

body.text: sadāmurttād amūrttādvā bhāvād yad vāpy abhāvataḥ &

children.text: uttheyān me praśastasya bhavatpūjāmahotsavaḥ // UtSst_17.46 //
children.translated_text: may the auspicious great festival of worshipping you arise for me. // UtSst_17.46 //

body.translated_text: From the ever-embodied or the formless, from being or indeed from non-being —

children.text: ye 'rcayanti namas tebhyas teṣāṃ tuṣṭo 'smi tattvataḥ // UtSst_17.47 //
children.translated_text: salutations to them; I am truly delighted with them. // UtSst_17.47 //

body.translated_text: Those who worship you always with desire, anger, and pride made into offerings —

children.text: yas tṛṇaiḥ kriyamāno 'pi ratnair evopakalpate // UtSst_17.48 //
children.translated_text: which, though performed with [mere] blades of grass, is equal to [worship] with jewels. // UtSst_17.48 //

body.translated_text: Victorious is this supreme mode of worship of those who possess devotion to you,
The eighteenth hymn, named 'Manifestation.'

body.text: jagato 'ntarato bhavantam āptvā punar etad bhavato 'ntarāl labhante &

children.text: jagadīśa tavaiva bhaktibhājo na hi teṣām iha dūrato 'sti kiñcit // UtSst_18.1 //
children.translated_text: O Lord of the world, those who possess devotion to you; for nothing here is far from them. // UtSst_18.1 //

body.translated_text: Having found you within the world, they again obtain this [world] from within you —

body.text: kvacid eva bhavān kvacid bhavānī sakalārthakramagarbhiṇī pradhānā &

children.text: paramārthapade tu naiva devyā bhavato nāpi jatattrayasya bhedaḥ // UtSst_18.2 //
children.translated_text: but in the plane of ultimate reality there is no difference of the Goddess from you, nor of the triad of born [principles]. // UtSst_18.2 //

body.translated_text: Somewhere [you appear as] yourself, somewhere as <s>Bhavānī</s>, pregnant with the entire succession of purposes, the principal one —

body.text: no jānate subhagam apy avalepavanto lokāḥ prayatnasubhagā nikhila hi bhāvāḥ &

children.text: cetaḥ punar yad idam udyatam apy avaiti naivātmarūpam iha hā tad aho hato 'smi // UtSst_18.3 //
children.translated_text: but this mind, though active, does not even know its own nature — alas, I am utterly destroyed! // UtSst_18.3 //

body.translated_text: The proud world does not know [you] even though you are auspicious, for all things are beautiful only through effort;

children.text: na bhojanācchādanam apy ajasram apekṣate yas tam ahaṃ nato 'smi // UtSst_18.4 //
children.translated_text: does not even constantly require food or clothing — to him I bow. // UtSst_18.4 //

body.translated_text: He who, having worshipped your feet with the abundance of wealth obtained by dwelling in his own Self which consists of you,

body.text: sadā bhavaddehanivāsasvastho 'py antaḥ paraṃ dahyata eṣa lokaḥ &

children.text: tavecchayā tat kuru me yathātra tvadarcanānandamayo bhaveyam // UtSst_18.5 //
children.translated_text: therefore, by your will, act so that I may here become full of the bliss of worshipping you. // UtSst_18.5 //

body.translated_text: This world, though always at ease dwelling in your body, is supremely burning within;

children.text: sakārthacayeṣv ahaṃ bhaveyam sukhasaṃsparśanamātralokayātraḥ // UtSst_18.6 //
children.translated_text: may I, amid the mass of worldly purposes, pursue the course of life through the mere touch of bliss. // UtSst_18.6 //

body.translated_text: With my mind absorbed in drinking the nectar of worship of your two lotus feet, arising from its own <s>rasa</s> (essence),

body.text: sakalavyavahāragocare sphuṭam antaḥ spurati tvayi prabho &

children.text: upayānty apayānti cāniśam mama vastūni vibhāntu sarvadā // UtSst_18.7 //
children.translated_text: may my things, which ceaselessly come and go, shine forth always. // UtSst_18.7 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, while you clearly pulsate within, in the range of all worldly dealings,

body.text: satatam eva tavaiva pure 'thavāpy arahito vicareyam ahaṃ tvayā &

children.text: kṣaṇalavo 'py atha mā sma bhavet sa me na vijaye nanu yatra bhavanmayaḥ // UtSst_18.8 //
children.translated_text: but let there not be even a fraction of a moment for me where, not being pervaded by you, I fail to be victorious. // UtSst_18.8 //

body.translated_text: May I always wander in your city alone, or even [if] abandoned by you;

children.text: bhavadarcanasampadeha bhaktās tava saṃsārasaro 'ntare caranti // UtSst_18.9 //
children.translated_text: which is filled on all sides with streams of cool, delightful nectar flowing from your limbs. // UtSst_18.9 //

body.translated_text: O wealth of worshipping you! Your devotees move within the lake of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: nijātmani sadā nātha vaseyaṃ tava pūjakaḥ // UtSst_18.10 //
children.translated_text: may I dwell always in my own Self, O Lord, as your worshipper. // UtSst_18.10 //

body.translated_text: In the coolness of the shade of the great <s>mantra</s>-tree, in your great forest,

children.text: mama nātha tathā puraḥ prathāṃ vraja netratrayaśūlaśobhitaḥ // UtSst_18.11 //
children.translated_text: so, O Lord, become manifest before me, adorned with three eyes and trident. // UtSst_18.11 //

body.translated_text: Just as you appear in every being, in all that lives, consisting of radiant awareness —

children.text: paritoṣagataḥ kadā bhavān mama sarvatra bhaved dṛśaḥ padam // UtSst_18.12 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, will you become the object of my vision everywhere? // UtSst_18.12 //

body.translated_text: When, having become pleased with the offering of ego's sacrifice, fashioned with the fullness of possessive devotion —

children.text: sakalaṃ janavṛttam ācareyaṃ rasayan sarvata eva kiñcanāpi // UtSst_18.13 //
children.translated_text: may I perform the entire course of worldly conduct, savoring everywhere something [of your essence]. // UtSst_18.13 //

body.translated_text: Dwelling in the midst of the ocean of supreme nectar, with my mind immersed solely in the rite of worshipping you,

body.text: bhavadīyam ihāstu vastu tattvaṃ vivarītuṃ ka ivātra pātram arthe &

children.text: idam eva hi nāmarūpaceṣṭādyasamaṃ te harate haro 'si yasmāt // UtSst_18.14 //
children.translated_text: For this very [truth] — incomparable in name, form, and activity — seizes [all], since you are <s>Hara</s> (the Seizer). // UtSst_18.14 //

body.translated_text: Let the reality here be your truth — who is a fit vessel to unveil it?

body.text: śāntaye na sukhalipsutā manāg bhaktisambhṛtamadeṣu taiḥ prabhoḥ &

children.text: mokṣamārgaṇaphalāpi nārthanā smaryate hṛdayahāriṇaḥ puraḥ // UtSst_18.15 //
children.translated_text: nor is the quest for liberation even remembered before the heart-stealer, the Lord. // UtSst_18.15 //

body.translated_text: For the sake of peace, there is not the slightest desire for pleasure among those intoxicated with devotion;

body.text: jāgaretaradaśāthavā parā yāpi kācana manāg avasthiteḥ &

children.text: bhaktibhājanajanasya sākhilā tvatsanāthamanaso mahotsavaḥ // UtSst_18.16 //
children.translated_text: for people who are vessels of devotion, whose minds are sheltered in you, all [of life] is a great festival. // UtSst_18.16 //

body.translated_text: Whether in waking or another state, or even in some supreme [state] slightly beyond [ordinary] existence —

children.text: tvām avāpya dṛḍhadīrghasaṃvido nātha bhaktidhanasoṣmaṇāṃ katham // UtSst_18.17 //
children.translated_text: how, O Lord, upon reaching you, [can they not] become firm and lasting in awareness, for those whose warmth is the wealth of devotion? // UtSst_18.17 //

body.translated_text: The activities of the circle of senses, from the mind onward — even those whose functions are everywhere loosened —

body.text: na ca vibhinnam asṛjyata kiñcid asty atha sukhetarad atra na nirmitam &

children.text: atha ca duḥkhi ca bhedi ca sarvathāpy asamavismayadhāma namo 'stu te // UtSst_18.18 //
children.translated_text: and yet there is suffering and division — O abode of incomparable wonder in every way, salutation to you! // UtSst_18.18 //

body.translated_text: Nothing was created as separate, nor was anything other than happiness fashioned here;

children.text: dalitadurjayasaṃśayavairiṇas tvadavalokanam astu nirantaram // UtSst_18.19 //
children.translated_text: nectar filling the pit of harsh negation, and whose invincible enemy of doubt has been shattered. // UtSst_18.19 //

body.translated_text: May the vision of you be unceasing for me, whose stain of mental constructs has been washed by the overflowing

body.text: sphuṭam aviśa mām athāviśeyaṃ satataṃ nātha bhavantamasmi yasmāt &

children.text: rabhasena vapus tavaiva sākṣāt paramāsattigataḥ samarcayeyam // UtSst_18.20 //
children.translated_text: so that with fervor, having attained supreme attachment, I may directly worship your very body. // UtSst_18.20 //

body.translated_text: Clearly enter me, or let me enter you constantly, O Lord, since I am [yours];

body.text: tvayi na stutiśaktir asti kasyāpy athavāsty eva yato 'tisundaro 'si &

children.text: satataṃ punar arthitaṃ mamaitad yad aviśrānti vilokayeyam īśam // UtSst_18.21 //
children.translated_text: but my constant prayer is this: that I may behold the Lord without rest. // UtSst_18.21 //

body.translated_text: No one has the power to praise you — or rather, everyone does, since you are supremely beautiful;
The nineteenth hymn, named 'Illumination.'

children.text: jayaty apūrvavṛttāntaḥ śivaḥ satkalpapādapaḥ // UtSst_19.1 //
children.translated_text: who bestows marvelous fruits that transcend the plane of prayer, whose ways are unprecedented. // UtSst_19.1 //

body.translated_text: Victorious is <s>Śiva</s>, the true wish-fulfilling tree,

body.text: sarvavastuni ca yaikanidhānāt svātmanas tvad akhilaṃ kila labhyam &

children.text: asya me punar asau nijā ātmā na tvam eva ghaṭase paramās tām // UtSst_19.2 //
children.translated_text: yet for me, this Self of mine does not manifest as you alone; may the supreme [realization] come to pass! // UtSst_19.2 //

body.translated_text: Since everything is indeed obtainable through you from the single treasury of one's own Self present in all things —

children.text: syād vapus tu nikhileṣu padārtheṣv eṣu nāma na bhavet kim utānyat // UtSst_19.3 //
children.translated_text: should there be [his] embodiment in all these objects — would that not be [evident]? What then to say of anything else? // UtSst_19.3 //

body.translated_text: The Self, whose body is consciousness composed of knowledge and action, is in every way the Supreme Lord alone;

children.text: abhilīya pathā nātha mamāstu tvanmayī gatiḥ // UtSst_19.4 //
children.translated_text: having dissolved upon the path, O Lord, may my course become one of being pervaded by you. // UtSst_19.4 //

body.translated_text: By this fruit whose nature is your vision, which steals away terrible suffering,

children.text: siddhajanamānasānāṃ vismayajananī ghaṭeta mama bhavataḥ // UtSst_19.5 //
children.translated_text: which generates wonder in the minds of perfected beings, come about for me from you? // UtSst_19.5 //

body.translated_text: When will that <s>siddhi</s> (perfection), adorned with the jewel-creeper of contemplation of your pure feet,

body.text: karhi nātha vimalaṃ mukhabimbaṃ tāvakaṃ samavalokayitāsmi &

children.text: yatsravaty amṛtapūram apūrvaṃ yo nimajjayati viśvam aśeṣam // UtSst_19.6 //
children.translated_text: which overflows with an unprecedented flood of nectar and submerges the entire world? // UtSst_19.6 //

body.translated_text: When, O Lord, shall I behold your pure face-orb,

body.text: dhyātamātramuditaṃ tava rūpaṃ karhi nātha paramāmṛtapūraiḥ &

children.text: pūrayet tvadavibhedavimokṣākhyātidūravivarāṇi sadā me // UtSst_19.7 //
children.translated_text: fill always for me, with floods of supreme nectar, the far-distant cavities known as liberation through non-difference from you? // UtSst_19.7 //

body.translated_text: When, O Lord, will your form, which arises merely through meditation,

children.text: nādyāpi me mano nātha karhi syād astu śīghrataḥ // UtSst_19.8 //
children.translated_text: [become steady]? Even today it has not — may it be so swiftly! // UtSst_19.8 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, when will my mind, having abandoned its fickleness through attachment to your unsurpassed <s>rasa</s> (essence),

body.text: mā śuṣkakaṭukāny eva paraṃ sarvāṇi sarvadā &

children.text: tavopahṛtya labdhāni dvandvāny apy āpatantu me // UtSst_19.9 //
children.translated_text: having been offered to you and [thus] obtained [back], may even the pairs of opposites befall me [as blessings]. // UtSst_19.9 //

body.translated_text: May not all things always be merely dry and bitter;

body.text: nātha sāṃmukhyam āyāntu viśuddhās tava raśmayaḥ &

children.text: yāvat kāyamanastāpatamobhiḥ parilupyatām // UtSst_19.10 //
children.translated_text: so that the darkness of the torment of body and mind may be destroyed. // UtSst_19.10 //

body.translated_text: O Lord, may your pure rays come to face me,

children.text: paramārthamuṣo vaśyā bhūyāsur guṇataskarāḥ // UtSst_19.11 //
children.translated_text: the thieves of virtue who steal ultimate reality, may be brought under control. // UtSst_19.11 //

body.translated_text: O God, be gracious, so that the obstacles on your path for me,

body.text: tvad bhaktisudhāsārair mānasam āpūryatāṃ mamāśu vibho &

children.text: yāvad imā uhyantāṃ niḥśeṣāsāravāsanāḥ plutvā // UtSst_19.12 //
children.translated_text: so that these entirely worthless latent impressions may be washed away, flooding [them] completely. // UtSst_19.12 //

body.translated_text: O all-pervading Lord, may my mind be quickly filled with the essential nectar of devotion to you,

body.text: mokṣadaśāyāṃ bhaktis tvayi kuta iva martyadharmiṇo 'pi na sā &

children.text: rājati tato 'nurūpām āropaya siddhibhūmikām aja mām // UtSst_19.13 //
children.translated_text: shine forth [fully]; therefore, O unborn one, elevate me to a fitting plane of perfection. // UtSst_19.13 //

body.translated_text: In the state of liberation, whence would there be devotion to you? Even that of one subject to mortality does not

body.text: siddhilavalābhalubdhaṃ mām avalepena mā vibho saṃsthāḥ &

children.text: kṣāmas tvadbhaktimukhe prollasadaṇimādipakṣato mokṣaḥ // UtSst_19.14 //
children.translated_text: liberation is slender compared to <s>aṇimā</s> (the power of minuteness) and the other [powers] that flash forth at the face of devotion to you. // UtSst_19.14 //

body.translated_text: O all-pervading Lord, do not regard me with disdain, greedy as I am for even a particle of <s>siddhi</s> (perfection);

body.text: dāsasya me prasīdatu bhagavān etāvad eva nanu yāce &

children.text: dātā tribhuvananātho yasya na tanmādṛśāṃ dṛśo viṣayaḥ // UtSst_19.15 //
children.translated_text: the giver is the Lord of the three worlds, whose [gift] is beyond the scope of vision of ones like me. // UtSst_19.15 //

body.translated_text: May the Blessed Lord be gracious to me, his servant — this much alone I ask;

children.text: māmake vikasad astu sadaiva prasravanmadhu kim apy atilokam // UtSst_19.16 //
children.translated_text: may the pair of your lotus feet forever blossom, exuding some supramundane honey. // UtSst_19.16 //

body.translated_text: In my mind, filled with the nectar-essence of the remembrance of your body,

body.text: asti me prabhur asau janako 'tha tryambako 'tha jananī ca bhavānī &

children.text: na dvitīya iha ko 'pi mamāstīty eva nirvṛtatamo vicareyam // UtSst_19.17 //
children.translated_text: 'there is no other for me here' — with this [thought], may I wander about in supreme contentment. // UtSst_19.17 //

body.translated_text: That Lord is my father — <s>Tryambaka</s> (the Three-eyed One) — and my mother is <s>Bhavānī</s>;
The twentieth hymn, named 'Savoring.'

children.text: upavītīkṛtabhoginam indukalāśekharaṃ vande // UtSst_20.1 //
children.translated_text: with a serpent as his sacred thread, crescent-moon-crested. // UtSst_20.1 //

body.translated_text: I praise the Lord, the master of the three worlds, white with ashes, three-eyed, bearing a trident,

children.text: vilasatkapālamālākalpitanṛttotsavākalpam // UtSst_20.2 //
children.translated_text: whose dance-festival adornment is fashioned with a shining garland of skulls. // UtSst_20.2 //

body.translated_text: I bow to him whose white raiment has the radiance of garments [shed] from his own body, surpassing recollection,

body.text: vande tān daivataṃ yeṣāṃ haraś ceṣṭā harocitāḥ &

children.text: haraikapravaṇāḥ prāṇāḥ sadā saubhāgyasadmanām // UtSst_20.3 //
children.translated_text: whose life-breaths are solely devoted to <s>Hara</s> — those who are always abodes of blessedness. // UtSst_20.3 //

body.translated_text: I salute those whose deity is <s>Hara</s>, whose actions are worthy of <s>Hara</s>,

body.text: krīḍitaṃ tava maheśvaratāyāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nyad idam eva yathaitat &

children.text: iṣṭamātraghaṭiteṣv avadāneṣv ātmanā param upāyam upaimi // UtSst_20.4 //
children.translated_text: in exploits accomplished by mere will alone, I know of no higher means than you yourself. // UtSst_20.4 //

body.translated_text: Your play of supreme lordship — everything else follows behind it, just as this [world does];

children.text: tava nātha kiyān bhūyānn ānandarasasambhavaḥ // UtSst_20.5 //
children.translated_text: O Lord, how much greater must be the arising of the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of bliss! // UtSst_20.5 //

body.translated_text: In this abode of yours, honored by all the world, with such play being present,

body.text: kathaṃ sa subhago mā bhūdyo gauryā vallabho haraḥ &

children.text: haro 'pi mā bhūd atha kiṃ gauryāḥ paramavallabhaḥ // UtSst_20.6 //
children.translated_text: Even if he were not <s>Hara</s>, what [does it matter]? — he is the supreme beloved of <s>Gaurī</s>. // UtSst_20.6 //

body.translated_text: How could he not be blessed — he who is <s>Hara</s>, the beloved of <s>Gaurī</s>?

children.text: saṃvillatās tathārūpās tasya kasyāpi sattaroḥ // UtSst_20.7 //
children.translated_text: the creepers of consciousness of that certain tree of existence are of such a form. // UtSst_20.7 //

body.translated_text: Whose [nature] is composed of the nectar of meditation, rooted in one's own Self, imperishable —

children.text: mahānikaṣapāṣāṇasthūṇā pūjaiva jāyate // UtSst_20.8 //
children.translated_text: worship itself becomes a great touchstone-pillar. // UtSst_20.8 //

body.translated_text: O Supreme Lord, at the occasion of exultant joy, when devotion is itching [to express itself],

children.text: sadā tribhuvanāhāratṛptāya svāmine namaḥ // UtSst_20.9 //
children.translated_text: always seated in the bliss of maintenance, always satisfied by the meal of the three worlds [in dissolution]. // UtSst_20.9 //

body.translated_text: Salutation to the Lord, who is always delighted by the sport of creation,

body.text: na kvāpi gatvā hitvāpi na kiṃcid idam eva ye &

children.text: bhavyaṃ tvaddhāma paśyanti bhavyās tebhyo namo namaḥ // UtSst_20.10 //
children.translated_text: as your auspicious abode — salutation upon salutation to those blessed ones! // UtSst_20.10 //

body.translated_text: Those who, without going anywhere and without abandoning anything, see this very [world]

children.text: etayā vā daridraṇāṃ kim anyad upayācitam // UtSst_20.11 //
children.translated_text: And for those impoverished of it, what else can be requested? // UtSst_20.11 //

body.translated_text: For those enriched with the splendor of devotion, what else need be requested?

body.text: duḥkhāny api sukhāyante viṣam apy amṛtāyate &

children.text: mokṣāyate ca saṃsāro yatra mārgaḥ sa śaṅkaraḥ // UtSst_20.12 //
children.translated_text: and even <s>saṃsāra</s> becomes liberation — that path is <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // UtSst_20.12 //

body.translated_text: Where even sufferings become pleasures, even poison becomes nectar,

body.text: mūle madhye 'vasāne ca nāsti duḥkhaṃ bhavajjuṣāṃ &

children.text: tathāpi vayam īśāna sīdāmaḥ katham ucyatām // UtSst_20.13 //
children.translated_text: yet even so, O <s>Īśāna</s>, we languish — let it be told how. // UtSst_20.13 //

body.translated_text: At the beginning, middle, and end, there is no suffering for those devoted to you;

children.text: prakāśaḥ svairiṇām iva bhavān bhaktimatāṃ prabho // UtSst_20.14 //
children.translated_text: but for the devoted, O Lord, you [manifest as] light [that comes] of its own accord, as freely [as to] the self-willed. // UtSst_20.14 //

body.translated_text: For others, [you are] to be sought through <s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) and the like;

body.text: bhaktānāṃ nārtayo nāpy asty ādhyānaṃ svātmanas tava &

children.text: tathāpy asti śivety etat kim apy eṣāṃ bahirmukhe // UtSst_20.15 //
children.translated_text: yet even so, there is something [that cries] 'O <s>Śiva</s>!' of theirs, turned outward. // UtSst_20.15 //

body.translated_text: Devotees have no afflictions, nor is there meditation on you as distinct from their own Self;

children.text: aham etad iti staumi tāṃ kriyāśaktim īśa te // UtSst_20.16 //
children.translated_text: [proclaiming] 'I am this' [about] everything — I praise that <s>kriyā-śakti</s> (power of action) of yours, O Lord. // UtSst_20.16 //

body.translated_text: That which shines forth as the appearance of all appearances, enveloped in reflective awareness,

children.text: grasamānās tato vande deva viśvaṃ bhavanmayam // UtSst_20.17 //
children.translated_text: being consumed [by time]; therefore I salute, O God, the universe as pervaded by you. // UtSst_20.17 //

body.translated_text: All beings dwell [in existence], even <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: evamevodyate nātha tvayā saṃhāralīlayā // UtSst_20.18 //
children.translated_text: thus indeed is it proclaimed, O Lord, by your play of dissolution. // UtSst_20.18 //

body.translated_text: Because of the connection of the existent with destruction, everything beyond me is false —

body.text: dhyātam ātmupatiṣṭhata eva tvadvapur varada bhaktidhanānām &

children.text: apy acintyam akhilādbhutacintākartṛtāṃ prati ca te vijayante // UtSst_20.19 //
children.translated_text: Even the inconceivable — regarding your authorship of all wondrous contemplation — they triumph! [UtSst 20.19]

body.translated_text: O boon-granter, your body, when meditated upon, establishes itself in the Self of those whose wealth is devotion,

children.text: nṛtyati vīrajano niśi vetālakulaiḥ kṛtotsāhaḥ // UtSst_20.20 //
children.translated_text: the heroic ones dance at night, inspired by hosts of <s>vetāla</s>s (spirits). [UtSst 20.20]

body.translated_text: As if sprinkled with the wine of the <s>rasa</s> (bliss) of devotion to you, with the throbbing of their gladdened vital centers,

body.text: ārabdhā bhavadabhinutir amunā yenāṅgakena mama śambho &

children.text: tenāparyantam imaṃ kālaṃ dṛḍham akhilam eva bhaviṣīṣṭa // UtSst_20.21 //
children.translated_text: may that limb, and indeed my entire being, endure firmly for all time without end. [UtSst 20.21]

body.translated_text: With whatever limb of mine this praise of you has been begun, O <s>Śambhu</s>,
